akhfash:15-16.t: He said ﴿كَلاَّ إِنَّهَا لَظَىٰ﴾ ﴿نَزَّاعَةً لِّلشَّوَىٰ﴾: accusative as a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ (the pronoun)**, and the khabar (predicate) of "إنَّ" is ﴿نزَاعةٌ﴾. «[Translator's note: so in the source; the text appears disturbed here, since it explains the accusative نَزَّاعَةً and then names the nominative نَزَّاعَةٌ as the predicate.]» And if you wish, you make ﴿لَظَى﴾ nominative as the khabar of ﴿إِنَّ﴾ and make "النزّاعة" nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).

akhfash:19-19.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً﴾, then He said ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ﴾: He made ﴿الإِنْسانَ﴾ a plurality, and what shows you this is that He has excepted a plurality from it.

akhfash:36-37.t: And He said ﴿فَمَالِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ قِبَلَكَ مُهْطِعِينَ﴾ ﴿عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ عِزِينَ﴾, just as you say "ما لَكَ قَائِماً" ("why are you standing?"). The singular of "العِزِينَ" is العِزَةُ (a band), like "ثُبَة" and "ثُبِين".

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿سَأَلَ سَائِلٌ﴾ a caller called for ﴿بِعَذَابٍ وَاقِعٍ﴾

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿لِلْكَافِرِينَ لَيْسَ لَهُ دَافِعٌ﴾ He is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who said: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth…" (the ayah).

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ connected to وَاقِعٍ ﴿ذِي الْمَعَارِجِ﴾ the ascending-places of the angels, namely the heavens.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿تَعْرُجُ﴾ read with tāʾ and with yāʾ ﴿الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ﴾ Gabriel ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ i.e. to the place where His command descends from the heaven ﴿فِي يَوْمٍ﴾ attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, i.e. the punishment befalls them on the Day of Resurrection ﴿كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ﴾ relative to the unbeliever, because of the hardships he meets in it; as for the believer, it will be lighter for him than a prescribed prayer he prays in this world, as has come in the hadith.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فَاصْبِرْ﴾ this was before he was commanded to fight ﴿صَبْرًا جَمِيلًا﴾ i.e. with no anxious complaint in it.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَهُ﴾ i.e. the punishment ﴿بَعِيدًا﴾ as not going to happen,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَنَرَاهُ قَرِيبًا﴾ as happening without any doubt.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿يَوْمَ تَكُونُ السَّمَاءُ﴾ attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, i.e. it befalls ﴿كَالْمُهْلِ﴾ like molten silver,

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَتَكُونُ الْجِبَالُ كَالْعِهْنِ﴾ like wool, in lightness and in flying about with the wind,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَلَا يَسْأَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيمًا﴾ a relative [does not ask about] his relative, because each is occupied with his own state.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ﴾ i.e. the close relatives are made to see one another, and they recognise one another but do not speak; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿يَوَدُّ الْمُجْرِمُ﴾ the unbeliever wishes ﴿لَوْ﴾ in the sense of أَنْ ﴿يَفْتَدِي مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ﴾ with kasra on the mīm and with fatḥa ﴿بِبَنِيهِ﴾

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَفَصِيلَتِهِ﴾ his clan, [so called] because he is separated (faṣl) from it ﴿الَّتِي تُؤْوِيهِ﴾ which gathers him in,

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ يُنْجِيهِ﴾ that ransoming; conjoined to يَفْتَدِي.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a rejection of what he wishes. ﴿إِنَّهَا﴾ i.e. the Fire ﴿لَظَى﴾ a name for Hell, because it blazes (tatalaẓẓā), i.e. flames up against the unbelievers,

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿نَزَّاعَةً لِلشَّوَى﴾ plural of شَوَاة, which is the skin of the head.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿تَدْعُوا مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّى﴾ from faith, by saying: "To me! To me!"

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَجَمَعَ﴾ wealth ﴿فَأَوْعَى﴾ held it in his container and did not pay Allah's due from it.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعًا﴾ an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial, ḥāl muqaddara), and its explanation is:

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿إِذَا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ جَزُوعًا﴾ at the time evil touches him,

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ الْخَيْرُ مَنُوعًا﴾ at the time good, i.e. wealth, touches him, withholding Allah's due from it,

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ فِي أَمْوَالِهِمْ حَقٌّ مَعْلُومٌ﴾ it is the zakat,

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿لِلسَّائِلِ وَالْمَحْرُومِ﴾ the one who refrains from asking out of modesty and so is deprived,

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ مِنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّهِمْ مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ fearful;

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّهِمْ غَيْرُ مَأْمُونٍ﴾ its descent [is not safe from].

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَافِظُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿إِلَّا عَلَى أَزْوَاجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ﴾ of slave women ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ﴾

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿فَمَنِ ابْتَغَى وَرَاءَ ذَلِكَ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْعَادُونَ﴾ those who overstep the lawful into the unlawful.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَمَانَاتِهِمْ﴾ — in one reading in the singular — what they have been entrusted with in matters of religion and of this world, ﴿وَعَهْدِهِمْ﴾ taken from them concerning that ﴿رَاعُونَ﴾ guardians,

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ بِشَهَادَتِهِمْ﴾ — in one reading in the plural [بِشَهَادَاتِهِمْ] — ﴿قَائِمُونَ﴾ they establish it and do not conceal it,

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَى صَلَاتِهِمْ يُحَافِظُونَ﴾ by performing it at its times;

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ مُكْرَمُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿فَمَالِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا قِبَلَكَ﴾ towards you ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. keeping their gaze fixed,

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ الشِّمَالِ﴾ of you ﴿عِزِينَ﴾ also a ḥāl, i.e. in groups, circle upon circle, saying in mockery of the believers: "If these enter Paradise, we shall surely enter it before them." Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿أَيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ يُدْخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a deterrent to them from their coveting Paradise. ﴿إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاهُمْ﴾ like others ﴿مِمَّا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ from sperm-drops; so Paradise is not to be coveted on that account, rather it is coveted only through piety (taqwā).

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿فَلَا﴾ the lā is redundant (zāʾida) ﴿أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ الْمَشَارِقِ وَالْمَغَارِبِ﴾ of the sun, the moon and all the stars ﴿إِنَّا لَقَادِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿عَلَى أَنْ نُبَدِّلَ﴾ bring in their place ﴿خَيْرًا مِنْهُمْ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ﴾ unable to do that.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿فَذَرْهُمْ﴾ leave them ﴿يَخُوضُوا﴾ in their falsehood ﴿وَيَلْعَبُوا﴾ in their worldly life ﴿حَتَّى يُلَاقُوا﴾ meet ﴿يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ﴾ the punishment in it,

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الْأَجْدَاثِ﴾ the graves ﴿سِرَاعًا﴾ to the place of gathering, ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَى نَصْبٍ﴾ — in one reading [نُصُبٍ] with ḍamma on both letters — something set up, such as a marker or a banner, ﴿يُوفِضُونَ﴾ hastening,

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿خَاشِعَةً﴾ abased ﴿أَبْصَارُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ﴾ covers them ﴿ذِلَّةٌ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمُ الَّذِي كَانُوا يُوعَدُونَ﴾ ذَلِكَ is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows it is the khabar (predicate), and it means the Day of Resurrection.

daas-irab:1-3.t: ﴿سَأَلَ سائِلٌ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِعَذابٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿واقِعٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of عذاب; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿لِلْكافِرينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to سأل. ﴿لَيْسَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of laysa. ﴿دافِعٌ﴾ the postponed noun of laysa; the clause is a second adjective of عذاب. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to واقع. ﴿ذِي﴾ an adjective of the Name of Majesty (Allah). ﴿الْمَعارِجِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿تَعْرُجُ الْمَلائِكَةُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَالرُّوحُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿فِي يَوْمٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to something omitted, its implied form being «occurs» (يقع). ﴿كانَ مِقْدارُهُ خَمْسِينَ﴾ kāna, its noun and its predicate. ﴿أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ﴾ tamyīz (specification), annexed to سنة; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of يوم.

daas-irab:5-7.t: ﴿فَاصْبِرْ صَبْراً﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿جَمِيلًا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿يَرَوْنَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the hāʾ is its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بَعِيداً﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَنَراهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its first mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿قَرِيباً﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:8-10.t: ﴿يَوْمَ تَكُونُ السَّماءُ﴾ an adverb of time, and a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb and its noun. ﴿كَالْمُهْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of تكون; المهل: molten silver; the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿وَتَكُونُ الْجِبالُ كَالْعِهْنِ﴾ the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf); العهن is wool. ﴿وَلا يَسْئَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيماً﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the second object is omitted, its implied form being «his intercession» (شفاعته); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the hāʾ is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of حميما. ﴿يَوَدُّ الْمُجْرِمُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لَوْ يَفْتَدِي﴾ law is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the interpreted maṣdar formed from law and the verb is the object of يود. ﴿مِنْ عَذابِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿يَوْمِئِذٍ﴾ يوم is an adverb of time annexed to its like. ﴿بِبَنِيهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يفتدي.

daas-irab:12-14.t: ﴿وَصاحِبَتِهِ وَأَخِيهِ﴾ both conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes them. ﴿وَفَصِيلَتِهِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ a relative noun, an adjective (ṣifa) of فصيلته. ﴿تُؤْوِيهِ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ conjoined to بنيه. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ثُمَّ يُنْجِيهِ﴾ thumma is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:15-18.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence (radʿ wa-zajr). ﴿إِنَّها﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَظى﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿نَزَّاعَةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لِلشَّوى﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نزاعة; الشوى is the plural of شواة, the skin of the head. ﴿تَدْعُوا﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿مَنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿أَدْبَرَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَتَوَلَّى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أدبر, and what follows it is conjoined to it.

daas-irab:19-21.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿خُلِقَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿هَلُوعاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿إِذا مَسَّهُ﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive, and a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الشَّرُّ﴾ its fāʿil (agent). ﴿جَزُوعاً﴾ khabar of an omitted kāna, omitted together with its noun; the omitted clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position, and the clause مسه is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿وَإِذا مَسَّهُ الْخَيْرُ مَنُوعاً﴾ the verse is conjoined (maʿṭūf).

daas-irab:22-23.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿الْمُصَلِّينَ﴾ excepted (mustathnā), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ badal (substitute) of المصلين. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿دائِمُونَ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين.

daas-irab:24-25.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding الذين. ﴿فِي أَمْوالِهِمْ حَقٌّ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate) and a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مَعْلُومٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿لِلسَّائِلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) معلوم. ﴿وَالْمَحْرُومِ﴾ conjoined to السائل.

daas-irab:26-28.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding الذين. ﴿يُصَدِّقُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿بِيَوْمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الدِّينِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ also conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنْ عَذابِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to مشفقون. ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is the ṣila of الذين. ﴿إِنَّ عَذابَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿غَيْرُ﴾ khabar of inna. ﴿مَأْمُونٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:29-29.t: The i'rab of its like has preceded in verse 27. [Translator's note: so in the source.]

daas-irab:30-30.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿عَلى أَزْواجِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) حافظون. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿ما﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أزواجهم. ﴿مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of causation (taʿlīl), and inna, its noun and its predicate, which is annexed to ملومين; the nominal clause is causal.

daas-irab:31-31.t: ﴿فَمَنِ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿من﴾ a conditional noun as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿ابْتَغى﴾ a past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿وَراءَ ذلِكَ﴾ an adverb of place, and the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَأُولئِكَ﴾ the fāʾ occurring in the apodosis of the condition. ﴿أولئك﴾ a demonstrative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿العادُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the two clauses of the condition are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من.

daas-irab:32-32.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لِأَماناتِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) راعون. ﴿وَعَهْدِهِمْ﴾ conjoined to أماناتهم. ﴿راعُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:33-33.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun, also conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بِشَهاداتِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them. ﴿قائِمُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:34-34.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to its like in the preceding verses. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them. ﴿يُحافِظُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:35-35.t: ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ the demonstrative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فِي جَنَّاتٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿مُكْرَمُونَ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:36-37.t: ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿ما﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لِ الَّذِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿قِبَلَكَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); مهطعين means: keeping their gaze fixed. ﴿عَنِ الْيَمِينِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَعَنِ الشِّمالِ﴾ both conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes them. ﴿عِزِينَ﴾ ḥāl; عزين means: in groups, circle upon circle.

daas-irab:38-38.t: ﴿أَيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving, rebuking interrogation, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), which is annexed to امرئ. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of امرئ. ﴿أَنْ يُدْخَلَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿جَنَّةَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿نَعِيمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to the verb يطمع; the clause «أيطمع..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:39-39.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence (radʿ wa-zajr). ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿خَلَقْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلقناهم. ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما.

daas-irab:40-40.t: ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿لا أُقْسِمُ﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿بِرَبِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْمَشارِقِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالْمَغارِبِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَقادِرُونَ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). ﴿قادرون﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:41-41.t: ﴿عَلى أَنْ نُبَدِّلَ﴾ a preposition, and an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by على, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) قادرون. ﴿خَيْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خيرا. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is of ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ما﴾ the Ḥijāzī negative mā. ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ its noun. ﴿بِمَسْبُوقِينَ﴾ genitive in form by the redundant (zāʾida) bāʾ, accusative in position as the khabar (predicate) of mā; the nominal clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:42-42.t: ﴿فَذَرْهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿يَخُوضُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿وَيَلْعَبُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يخوضوا. ﴿حَتَّى يُلاقُوا﴾ حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition, and an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after حتى, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿يَوْمَهُمُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by حتى, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يلعبوا. ﴿يُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:43-43.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ﴾ badal (substitute) of يومهم, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿مِنَ الْأَجْداثِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿سِراعاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ﴾ كأن and its noun. ﴿إِلى نُصُبٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what follows them. ﴿يُوفِضُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; يوفضون: they hasten; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of كأن, and the nominal clause is a second ḥāl.

daas-irab:44-44.t: ﴿خاشِعَةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَبْصارُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil (agent) of خاشعة. ﴿تَرْهَقُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ذِلَّةٌ﴾ a postponed fāʿil; the verbal clause is a second ḥāl. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ the demonstrative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْيَوْمُ﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of اليوم. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿يُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause «كانوا..» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.

dervis-irab:1-10.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْمَعارِجِ) the ascents (al-maṣāʿid), plural of مَعْرَج.
(المهل): the dregs of oil, or molten silver; it was mentioned before in Sūrat al-Dukhān.
(العهن) wool in general, without restriction, or wool dyed red, or dyed in various colours; these are different views.

* I'rab:
(سَأَلَ سائِلٌ بِعَذابٍ واقِعٍ) سأل is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, containing the meaning of دعا ("called for"), and for that reason it was made transitive the way that verb is; سائل is its agent (fāʿil); بعذاب is attached to (mutaʿalliq) سأل, and واقع is an adjective (naʿt). It is also said that it is in its own sense and the bāʾ has the meaning of عن ("about"); Abū al-Baqāʾ chose this. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said: «If it is from questioning (al-suʾāl), then its basis is to take two objects, and it is permissible to limit it to one of them; and if it is limited to one of them, it may take it by means of a preposition, so the implied form would be: a questioner asked Allah, or the Prophet ﷺ, or the Muslims, بعذاب, i.e. about a punishment». The questioner is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, when he said: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down stones upon us from the sky or bring us a painful punishment"; he was among those killed on the day of Badr. Al-Wāḥidī said: «The bāʾ in بعذاب is for emphasis, as in His words وهزي إليك بجذع النخلة, and the meaning is: a questioner asked for a punishment that will befall». (لِلْكافِرينَ لَيْسَ لَهُ دافِعٌ) Concerning the preposition and its genitive noun there are several views. The first is that it is attached to سأل as containing the meaning of دعا, i.e. he called for it upon them. The second is that it is attached to واقع and the lām is causal, i.e. descending because of them. The third is that the lām has the meaning of على, i.e. befalling the disbelievers; on this view it is also attached to واقع. The clause ليس له دافع is a second adjective of عذاب, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from عذاب because it is qualified. ليس is a defective past verb, له is its fronted khabar (predicate) and دافع its delayed noun. (مِنَ اللَّهِ ذِي الْمَعارِجِ) attached to واقع, i.e. befalling from Him and from His direction; or attached to دافع, meaning that there is none to repel it from His side when its time comes. ذي المعارج is an adjective of الله. (تَعْرُجُ الْمَلائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ إِلَيْهِ فِي يَوْمٍ كانَ مِقْدارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ) a resumptive statement, set out to emphasise the far-reaching loftiness. تعرج الملائكة is an imperfect verb and its agent; الروح is conjoined to الملائكة, and by it is meant Jibrīl, so it is a conjoining of the particular to the general. إليه is attached to تعرج; في يوم is attached to an omitted element indicated by واقع, i.e. the punishment befalls them on the Day of Resurrection. Kāna and its noun, and خمسين is its khabar; ألف سنة is the tamyīz (specification) of خمسين. Or [في يوم] is also attached to تعرج. (فَاصْبِرْ صَبْراً جَمِيلًا) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ, i.e. if you have known this and pondered its import, then be patient. اصبر is an imperative verb and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta"; صبرا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and جميلا an adjective. (إِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَهُ بَعِيداً) Inna and its noun, and the clause يرونه is its khabar; the pronoun is for the punishment; بعيدا is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because the seeing is cognitive. The clause is causal and has no grammatical position. (وَنَراهُ قَرِيباً) conjoined to the previous clause and falling within the scope of the khabar. (يَوْمَ تَكُونُ السَّماءُ كَالْمُهْلِ) The adverb is attached to قريبا, or to an omitted element indicated by واقع, i.e. it befalls on the day when … The clause تكون is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it; السماء is its noun and كالمهل its khabar. (وَتَكُونُ الْجِبالُ كَالْعِهْنِ) conjoined to the previous clause and parallel to it in its i'rab. (وَلا يَسْئَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيماً) The wāw is a conjunction and lā is negative; يسأل حميم is an imperfect verb and its agent; حميما is the first object of يسأل, and the second object is omitted, its implied form being "his intercession and his help". It is also said that حميما is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and يسأل then has no need of an object.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «يوم تعرج الملائكة والروح إليه في يوم كان مقداره خمسين ألف سنة» [Translator's note: the source quotes the verse with an initial «يوم», which is not in the Qur'anic text (تعرج الملائكة والروح إليه في يوم كان مقداره خمسين ألف سنة)] there is the device of figurative representation (tamthīl). What is meant is not the literal reality of that number; rather, what is meant is an indication that it will appear long to the disbeliever because of the terror and hardships he meets during it. So there is no contradiction with the verse of al-Sajda «في يوم كان مقداره ألف سنة». The Arabs describe days of hardship as long and days of joy as short. A poet said:
فقصارهنّ مع الهموم طويلة ... وطوالهنّ مع السرور قصار
(Their short ones, amid cares, are long, and their long ones, amid joy, are short.)
And another said:
ويوم كظل الرمح قصر طوله ... دم الزق عنا واصطفاق المزاهر
(And a day like the shadow of a spear, whose length was shortened for us by the blood of the wineskin and the clapping of lutes.)
2- In His words «يوم تكون السماء كالمهل» there is an unqualified simile (tashbīh mursal), and the point of resemblance is the changing of colour; likewise His words «وتكون الجبال كالعهن», where the point of resemblance is the flying about and scattering. Abū al-ʿAlāʾ cast his eyes on this lofty sky of eloquence when he said, lamenting his father:
فيا ليت شعري هل يخفّ وقاره ... إذا صار أحد في القيامة كالعهن
(Would that I knew: will his dignity grow light when Uḥud becomes like carded wool on the Day of Resurrection?)

dervis-irab:11-23.t:
* Vocabulary:
«وفصيلته» al-faṣīla is the clan (al-ʿashīra). Thaʿlab said: the nearest forefathers. It is a faʿīla with the meaning of a mafʿūla, i.e. one from whom [he] was separated.
(لَظى) a name of Hell, because it تتلظّى, i.e. blazes upon whoever roasts in it.
(لِلشَّوى) al-shawā is the plural of shawāt, which is the skin of the head (the scalp).

* I'rab:
(يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ يَوَدُّ الْمُجْرِمُ لَوْ يَفْتَدِي مِنْ عَذابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ بِبَنِيهِ) The clause is resumptive or circumstantial; al-Zamakhsharī permitted it to be an adjective, i.e. "a close friend made to see [them]". يبصرونهم is an imperfect passive verb; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and the hāʾ is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It was made to reach a second object by the doubling [of the middle radical], and the first object stood in place of the agent. The two pronouns in يبصرونهم were made plural, though they are for the two close friends, by construing them according to the meaning of generality, because they are two indefinite nouns in a negative context. In this there is evidence that the agent and the object occurring in a negative context are general, just as it was held regarding the words "By Allah, I will not drink water from a leather flask" that it covers all waters and all flasks, contrary to some regarding the flask. That is, the healthy ones are shown one another and recognise one another, but they do not exchange words because they are preoccupied with themselves. يود المجرم is an imperfect verb and its agent, and the clause is circumstantial; law is maṣdariyya with the meaning of an, because it occurs after a verb of wishing, and together with what falls in its scope it is an interpreted maṣdar, the object of يودّ, i.e. he wishes a ransoming. من عذاب is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يفتدي. يومئذ are two adverbs in construct, and the tanwīn is a substitute for omitted clauses, the implied form being: on the day when the sky becomes like molten metal, the mountains become like wool, and no close friend asks a close friend. ببنيه is also attached to يفتدي. (وَصاحِبَتِهِ وَأَخِيهِ وَفَصِيلَتِهِ الَّتِي تُؤْوِيهِ) conjoined to بنيه; the clause تؤويه is the ṣila (relative clause), i.e. which embraces him in lineage. (وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً ثُمَّ يُنْجِيهِ) also conjoined; في الأرض is the ṣila of the relative noun, and جميعا is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ثم is a conjunction of delay, on account of the severity of the terror; ينجيه is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object, i.e. he wishes that he could ransom himself and then that the ransom would save him. Thumma is for the remoteness of the saving; that is, he wishes that all these were within reach of his hand and that he could give them up in ransom for himself; but how far that is! (كَلَّا إِنَّها لَظى) كلا is a particle of rebuff and deterrence against their wish to ransom themselves, and an alert that that wish is not admissible and is of no avail. Inna and its noun, and لظى is its khabar (predicate); the pronoun is for the Fire, indicated by "the punishment". (نَزَّاعَةً لِلشَّوى) an emphatic or clarifying ḥāl, or it is accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) for intimidation. On the ḥāl view, what governs it is the verbal meaning indicated by لظى, i.e. it blazes as a stripper [of the scalp]. It was also read in the nominative, so it is a second khabar, i.e. [or] the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is a stripper"; it is said it is a badal (substitute) from لظى; it is said both are khabars; and it is said لظى is a badal from the noun of inna and نزّاعة is its khabar. (تَدْعُوا مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّى) The clause is a ḥāl from the pronoun in نزّاعة; the agent of تدعو is latent, referring to لظى; من is a relative noun, the direct object; the clause أدبر has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila, and تولّى is conjoined to أدبر. Further clarification of this calling will come in the section on rhetoric. (وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعى) conjoined to أدبر and تولّى. The meaning of أوعى is: he amassed wealth, put it in a container (wiʿāʾ) and hoarded it, and did not pay with it the right of Allah the Exalted. (إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً) The clause serves as the reason for what preceded. Inna and its noun; the al in الإنسان is generic; the clause خلق is the khabar of inna and the deputy agent is latent, referring to الإنسان; هلوعا is a prospective ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because he is not characterised by these qualities before his birth and at the time of his creation. (إِذا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ جَزُوعاً) إذا is an adverb attached to جزوعا; the clause مسّه is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it; الشر is the agent; جزوعا is a ḥāl from the pronoun in هلوعا, and you may make it an adjective of هلوعا. (وَإِذا مَسَّهُ الْخَيْرُ مَنُوعاً) conjoined to the previous clause and parallel to it in its i'rab. (إِلَّا الْمُصَلِّينَ) an exception from الإنسان, by which the genus is meant, so it is a connected exception. (الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ دائِمُونَ) الذين is an adjective of المصلين; هم is a mubtadaʾ; على صلاتهم is attached to دائمون, and دائمون is their khabar; the nominal clause is the ṣila of الذين.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «تدعو من أدبر وتولى» there is a rational metaphor (majāz ʿaqlī) for bringing them forth, as though it calls them and brings them forth — the discussion of rational metaphor has preceded in this book — or an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya). Of this kind is the saying of Dhū al-Rumma describing a wild bull:
أمسى بوهبين مجتازا لمرتعه ... من ذي الفوارس تدعو أنفه الربب
(At evening he was at Wahbayn, passing on to his pasture from Dhū al-Fawāris, the first sprouts calling his nose.)
Wahbayn is the name of a place, and likewise Dhū al-Fawāris. الربب, with two bāʾs, is the plural of rubba, which is the first pasture-grass to sprout. Al-duʿāʾ is requesting, and here it is a metaphor for causing the matter, because the small plants are the cause of his nose reaching the ground to graze on them. The calling may also be of the type of metaphor (istiʿāra): the sprouts are likened to a caller, the thing likened to is omitted, and something of its characteristics is taken.
Also of this kind is the saying of Dhū al-Rumma:
ليالي اللهو يطبيني فأتبعه ... كأنني ضارب في غمرة لعب
(Nights when amusement calls me and I follow it, as though I were a swimmer in a deep flood, playing.)
ليالي is accusative as an adverb; اللهو is a mubtadaʾ; طباه يطبوه ويطبيه when he calls him and draws him. That is, amusement calls me on many nights and I follow it, as though I were swimming in a deep expanse of water that covers a man's height. لعب is a second khabar. The adverb is attached to يطبيني, and it is said it is attached to what precedes it, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it.

dervis-irab:24-35.t:
* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ فِي أَمْوالِهِمْ حَقٌّ مَعْلُومٌ) والذين is conjoined to the first الذين; في أموالهم is a fronted khabar (predicate) and حق a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); معلوم is an adjective (naʿt). What is meant by it is the obligatory zakāt. The nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (لِلسَّائِلِ وَالْمَحْرُومِ) an adjective of حق. (وَالَّذِينَ يُصَدِّقُونَ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ) also conjoined; the clause يصدقون is the ṣila of the relative noun, and بيوم الدين is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يصدقون, i.e. the Day of Recompense. (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ مِنْ عَذابِ رَبِّهِمْ مُشْفِقُونَ) also conjoined; هم is a mubtadaʾ and مشفقون its khabar; من عذاب ربهم is attached to His word مشفقون; the clause is the ṣila. (إِنَّ عَذابَ رَبِّهِمْ غَيْرُ مَأْمُونٍ) The clause gives the reason for the fearing. Inna and its noun, and غير مأمون is its khabar. (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حافِظُونَ) also conjoined; هم is a mubtadaʾ and حافظون its khabar; لفروجهم is attached to حافظون, i.e. [guarding them] from the unlawful and forbidden. (إِلَّا عَلى أَزْواجِهِمْ أَوْ ما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ) إلا is a particle of exception, and على أزواجهم is an exception from the most general of states; aw is a conjunction and ما is conjoined to أزواجهم; the clause ملكت is the ṣila and أيمانهم is the fāʿil (agent). What is meant by ما ملكت أيمانهم is slave-women. فإنهم: the fāʾ is a conjunction; inna and its noun, and غير ملومين is its khabar. (فَمَنِ ابْتَغى وَراءَ ذلِكَ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ العادُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; من is a conditional noun causing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ; ابتغى is a past verb in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to من. وراء is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ابتغى, وراء having left its adverbial use, i.e. he sought what is beyond that, namely enjoyment by marriage and by what the right hand possesses. You may also keep it adverbial and attach it to an omitted element that is an adjective of the omitted direct object, i.e. whoever seeks a matter that lies beyond that. The fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); أولئك is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), and العادون is the khabar of أولئك; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. You may also make هم a second mubtadaʾ and العادون its khabar, the clause being the khabar of أولئك. (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَماناتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ راعُونَ) conjoined to what preceded; هم is a mubtadaʾ and راعون its khabar; لأماناتهم is attached to راعون; the nominal clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ بِشَهاداتِهِمْ قائِمُونَ) also conjoined; in one reading it is in the singular. (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ يُحافِظُونَ) also conjoined. (أُولئِكَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ مُكْرَمُونَ) أولئك is a mubtadaʾ, في جنات a khabar and مكرمون a second khabar; you may also attach في جنات to مكرمون.

* Rhetoric:
In the repetition of the prayer there is an evident hyperbole, out of concern for its importance and to extol its merit. Added to the repetition are: opening the clause with the pronoun and building the clause upon it, putting the preposition and its genitive noun before the verb, and the khabar's being a verbal clause. The nominal clause conveys permanence and continuity, and the verbal clause conveys renewal together with continuity. This is a wondrous pattern unique to the Book of Allah.

dervis-irab:36-44.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُهْطِعِينَ) hastening towards you, stretching out their necks, turning their gazes towards you. It is one of the words whose explanation needs whole sentences. In al-Qāmūs:
«هطع, like منع, هَطْعًا and هُطُوعًا: he hastened forward in fear, and turned his gaze on a thing, not taking it off it. هطع: he stretched out his neck and lowered his head, like استهطع. Like أمير [i.e. هطيع]: the wide road. Like محسن [i.e. مُهطِع]: one who looks in abasement and submission, not taking his gaze away; or the silent one who sets off towards whoever called him. A مُهطِع camel is one with a natural downward slope in its neck». The explanation of this root has preceded in Sūrat Ibrāhīm.
(عِزِينَ) plural of عِزَة. Abū ʿUbayda said: groups in dispersion. It is said: a small gathering, such as three by three and four by four. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "In the house there are عزون", i.e. various sorts of people. Al-Kumayt said:
ونحن وجندل باغ تركنا ... كتائب جندل شتّى عزينا
(We — and Jandal was the aggressor — left the troops of Jandal scattered in separate bands.)
عِزَة is one of the words whose final radical has been dropped. It is said it is a wāw and its origin is عِزْوَة, as though each group traces its descent (taʿtazī) to someone other than the one the other group traces its descent to, so they are dispersed; one says عزاه يعزوه when he attributes him to someone else. It is said its final radical is a hāʾ and the origin is عِزْهَة. عزة was given the plural with wāw and nūn just as سنة and its sisters were given the plural with them. It is also said it is a yāʾ, since one says عزيته, with yāʾ, أعزيه, with the meaning of عزوته. The discussion of what is attached to the sound masculine plural has preceded.
(نُصُبٍ) The discussion of it has preceded in detail, and we add here that it was read نَصْب, with fatḥa and sukūn; our reading is with two ḍammas; it was read with two fatḥas; and it was read with ḍamma then sukūn. The first is a singular noun with the meaning of the set-up marker towards which a person hastens. Abū ʿAmr said: it is the hunter's net, to which he hastens when game falls into it, for fear of its escaping. As for the second, it admits three views: first, that it is a singular noun with the meaning of an idol set up for worship; second, that it is the plural of نِصاب, like كُتُب, the plural of كتاب; third, that it is the plural of نَصْب, like رُهُن from رَهْن and سُقُف from سَقْف, and the plural of the plural is أنصاب. As for the third, it is a faʿal with the meaning of a mafʿūl, i.e. set up (manṣūb), like القَبَض with the meaning of المقبوض. The fourth is a lightened form of the second.
(يُوفِضُونَ) hastening to the caller, racing one another.

* I'rab:
(فَمالِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا قِبَلَكَ مُهْطِعِينَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; ما is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and للذين is the khabar (predicate) of ما, i.e. what is it that has befallen them and driven them to look at you and to disperse? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray at the Kaʿba and recite the Qur'an, and they would gather round him in circle after circle, listening and mocking his words, and saying: "If these enter Paradise as Muhammad says, we shall surely enter it before them"; so [this verse] was revealed. قبلك is an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), or to مهطعين, i.e. being in the direction that adjoins you, on the right and on the left. مهطعين is a ḥāl from الذين. (عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ الشِّمالِ عِزِينَ) The preposition and its genitive noun is also a ḥāl from the relative noun; it is said it is attached to مهطعين. عزين is also a ḥāl from the relative noun, so the four are ḥāls from the relative noun. It is also said it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in مهطعين, so it would be an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila). Abū al-Baqāʾ attached عن اليمين وعن الشمال to عزين, and some parsed عزين as an adjective of مهطعين. (أَيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ يُدْخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍ) The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval; يطمع is an imperfect verb and كل امرئ its fāʿil (agent); منهم is an adjective of امرئ. An and what falls in its scope is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to يطمع, i.e. does he covet entering? The nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of يدخل is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa", and جنة نعيم is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), by extension of usage. (كَلَّا إِنَّا خَلَقْناهُمْ مِمَّا يَعْلَمُونَ) كلا is a particle of rebuff and deterrence against their Ashʿab-like greed to enter Paradise [Translator's note: Ashʿab was a proverbial figure of greed]. The clause إنا خلقناهم gives the reason for the rebuff. Inna and its noun, and the clause خلقناهم is its khabar; مما is attached to خلقناهم, and the clause يعلمون is the ṣila (relative clause). The meaning is that they are created from a filthy drop of fluid that does not befit the world of holiness; so whoever has not adorned himself with faith, washed away the filth from himself with righteous deeds and added the perfections, is not worthy of entering the Gardens. Or it is an inference from the first creation to the second creation, and that the One who was able to create the first time is not incapable of bringing back. (فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ الْمَشارِقِ وَالْمَغارِبِ إِنَّا لَقادِرُونَ) The fāʾ is resumptive and lā is redundant (zāʾida); أقسم is an imperfect verb and its agent is latent, its implied form being "anā"; برب المشارق والمغارب is attached to أقسم. The clause إنا لقادرون has no grammatical position because it is the answer of the oath; inna and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and قادرون is its khabar. (عَلى أَنْ نُبَدِّلَ خَيْراً مِنْهُمْ وَما نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ) An and what falls in its scope is in the position of the genitive by على, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to قادرون; خيرا is the object of نبدل and منهم is attached to خيرا. The wāw is a conjunction; mā is Ḥijāzī and نحن is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition and مسبوقين is genitive in form and accusative in position as its khabar. The clause is conjoined to the answer of the oath and falls within what is sworn upon. (فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُوا وَيَلْعَبُوا حَتَّى يُلاقُوا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ, i.e. since it has become clear that bringing down upon them what We wish does not escape Us nor is beyond Our power, then leave them. ذرهم is an imperative verb whose past tense has died out, with a latent agent and a direct object; يخوضوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer of the command; يلعبوا is conjoined to يخوضوا. حتى is a particle of limit and of the genitive; يلاقوا is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after حتى, and the wāw is the agent; يومهم is the direct object and الذي an adjective of يومهم; the clause يوعدون is the ṣila of the relative noun; it is an imperfect passive verb and the wāw is the deputy agent. (يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الْأَجْداثِ سِراعاً كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلى نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ)
يوم is a badal (substitute) from يومهم; the clause يخرجون is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it; من الأجداث is attached to يخرجون; سراعا is a ḥāl from the wāw; the clause كأنهم is a second ḥāl, also from the wāw, so they would be successive ḥāls (mutarādifa), or from the pronoun in سراعا, so it would be an overlapping ḥāl. Kaʾanna and its noun; إلى نصب is attached to يوفضون, and the clause يوفضون is the khabar of كأنهم. (خاشِعَةً أَبْصارُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ ذلِكَ الْيَوْمُ الَّذِي كانُوا يُوعَدُونَ) خاشعة is a ḥāl from the agent of يوفضون or from the agent of يخرجون, the first being closer; أبصارهم is the agent of خاشعة. The clause ترهقهم ذلة is a second ḥāl, and you may make it resumptive. ذلك is a mubtadaʾ and اليوم its khabar, and الذي is an adjective; kāna and its noun, and the clause يوعدون is its khabar, and the clause is the ṣila. The clause ذلك اليوم is resumptive or explicative; in either case it has no grammatical position.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying: ﴿سَأَلَ سَآئِلٌ﴾.
A caller called for a punishment bound to fall. He was al-Naḍr [ibn al-Ḥārith] ibn Kalada; he said: O Allah, if what Muḥammad says is the truth from You, then rain stones upon us from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment. He was taken captive on the day of Badr and was executed in bonds (ṣabran), he and ʿUqba.
His saying: ﴿بِعَذَابٍ وَاقِعٍ﴾.
He means: for the unbelievers. الواقع is an adjective (naʿt) of العذاب, and the lām in الكافرين is attached to العذاب, not to الواقع.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿ولا يَسْأَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيماً﴾.
A relative will not ask about his relative; but they are made to recognise them [in the passive voice] for an hour, and then there is no mutual recognition after that hour. Some read: (ولا يُسْأَلُ حَميمٌ حَمِيماً): a close friend will not be asked: Where is your friend? I do not favour that, because it goes against the interpretation, and because the readers are agreed on (يَسأَل).

farraa:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿وَفَصِيلَتِهِ﴾: it is the smallest [i.e. nearest] of his ancestral lines, the one to which he traces his descent.

farraa:14-15.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ﴾, that is: [that] the ransom might save him from Allah's punishment.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿كَلاَّ﴾, that is: that will not save him. Then He began afresh and said: ﴿إِنَّهَا لَظَىٰ﴾. Laẓā is one of the names of Hell; for that reason He did not make it fully declinable (lam yujrihi).

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿نَزَّاعَةٌ لِّلشَّوَىٰ﴾.
It is nominative according to your saying: إنها لظى، إنها نزاعة للشوى (it is Laẓā; it is a stripper-off of the scalp). Or, if you wish, you may make the هاء a support pronoun (ʿimād), and make لظى nominative by نزاعة and نزاعة by لظى, as you say in speech: إِنَّه جاريتُك فارهة and إنها جاريتُك فارهة (your slave-girl is lively). The هاء in both ways is ʿimād. الشَّوَى are the hands and the feet; the scalp is called شواة; and whatever is not a fatal spot is شوًى.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿تَدْعُو مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ﴾.
It says to the unbeliever: O unbeliever, to me! O hypocrite, to me! So it calls each one by his name.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعَىٰ﴾.
He is saying: he gathered and hoarded — put it in a container (wiʿāʾ) — and paid no zakat from it and did not maintain ties of kinship.

farraa:19-22.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً﴾.
الهلوع is the impatient, and his description is as Allah said: ﴿إِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ جَزُوعاً﴾ ﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلْخَيْرُ مَنُوعاً﴾; this is the description of the هلوع. From it one says: هلِع يهلَع هلَعاً, like جزِع يجزَع جزعا. Then He said: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ﴾, excepting those who pray from الإنسان, because الإنسان is in the sense of a plural, as Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِنَّ الإِنْسَانَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ، إِلاَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿حَقٌّ مَعْلُومٌ﴾.
[It is] the zakat. Some said: No, rather it is something other than the zakat.

farraa:29-30.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ عَلَىٰ أَزْوَاجِهِمْ﴾.
Someone may ask: Is it permissible in speech to say: مررت بالقوم إِلاَّ بزيد (I passed by the people except by Zayd), meaning: except that I did not pass by Zayd? I said: That is not permissible; but what is in the Book of Allah is correct and good, because the beginning of the statement there is like a prohibition, since it was mentioned: ﴿والَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَافِظُون﴾. He is saying: they are not blamed except with regard to those other than their wives; so the statement proceeds according to ملومين at its end. Similar to it is your saying to a man: Do what you like except [for] killing a soul, for you will be punished — or: [except] in killing a soul; its meaning is: except that you will be punished for killing a soul.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿ذِي ٱلْمَعَارِجِ﴾.
It is an attribute of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because the angels ascend to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; so He described Himself by that.

farraa:37-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ عِزِينَ﴾.
العزون are circles, groups. They used to gather around the Prophet ﷺ and say: If these enter Paradise, as Muḥammad ﷺ says, we will surely enter it before them, and we will surely have more in it than they have. So Allah sent down: ﴿أَيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِىءٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُدْخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍ﴾.
The people read: "أن يُدخَل", with its agent unnamed (i.e. passive) [217/a]; and al-Ḥasan read: "أن يَدخُلَ", assigning the verb to him. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made clear and said [in effect]: Why do they despise them, when We created them all "from what they know" — from dust?

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ﴾.
He is saying: if others than the angels were to ascend, they would ascend in the span of fifty thousand years. As for (يعرج), the readers are agreed on tāʾ [تعرج]. One of the shaykhs mentioned, from Zuhayr, from Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh read "يعرج" with yāʾ. And al-Aʿmash said: I have never heard anyone read it except with tāʾ. Both are correct.

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلَىٰ نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ﴾. الإيفاض is hastening. The poet said:
لأنْعتنْ نعامةً ميفاضا * خَرْجاءَ ظلت تطلبُ الإضاضَا
(I will surely describe a swift ostrich, of two colours, that kept seeking a refuge.)
He said: خرجاء refers to colour: when a white shirt is patched with a red patch, it is أخرج. تطلب الإضاضا: i.e. she seeks a place to enter and take refuge in. Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read: "إلى نَصْبٍ": to something set up, towards which they race. Zayd ibn Thābit read: "إلى نُصُب يوفضون", as if النُّصُب were the gods that were worshipped [besides Allah]. Both are correct, and it is a singular; the plural is أنصاب.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَهُ بَعِيداً﴾.
He means the Resurrection; and We see it as near, because everything that is coming is near.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «بعذاب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سأل», and «سأل» includes the meaning of the verb «دعا» (to call for).

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «للكافرين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {سَأَلَ} in the sense of «دعا», i.e.: a caller called down upon the disbelievers a punishment bound to fall.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {دَافِعٌ}; «ذي» is a naʿt (adjective) of the Divine Name.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «تعرج الملائكة» is resumptive; the two preposition and its genitive nouns «إليه» and «في يوم» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تعرج»; the clause «كان» is a naʿt (adjective) of «يوم»; «ألف» is tamyīz (specification), and «سنة» is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «إنهم يرونه» is resumptive, and «بعيدا» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The adverb «يوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) {قَرِيبًا}.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «ولا يسأل» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {تَكُونُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «يُبَصَّرونهم» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «يودّ»; «لو» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «يومئذ»: «يوم» is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and «إذٍ» is an adverbial noun, a muḍāf ilayhi.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: «من» is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «فصيلته»; «جميعا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause); the clause «ينجيه» is conjoined to the clause {يَفْتَدِي}.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «كلا إنها لظى» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t:
«نزاعة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in {لَظَى}, because, although it is a proper name, it is treated like derived words, since it has the meaning of blazing (التلظِّي).

«للشوى» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «نزاعة», and the lām is redundant (zāʾida), for strengthening.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «تدعو» is a second khabar (predicate) of «إن» in verse «15».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: (إن الإنسان خلق هلوعا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; «هلوعا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: «إذا» is a pure adverb in both places; {جَزُوعًا} and «منوعا» are two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the pronoun in {هَلُوعًا}, the implied form being: anxious, being impatient at the time evil touches him, and «منوعا» [withholding] at the time good touches him.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: «المصلِّين» is excepted from {الإِنْسَانَ} in verse (19), which denotes the genus.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: «الذين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «المصلين»; the preposition and its genitive noun «على صلاتهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «دائمون».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The ṣila (relative clause) is the nominal clause «حق معلوم في أموالهم».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «للسائل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second naʿt (adjective) of {حَقٌّ}.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من عذاب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مشفقون».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: (إن عذاب ربهم غير مأمون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is parenthetical.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: His words «والذين»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the relative noun in verse (27); «لفروجهم» is the object of «حافظون», and the lām is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: (إلا على أزواجهم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The excepted [noun] is omitted, i.e.: guarding them (حِفْظَها); the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) maṣdar (verbal noun) (حِفْظَها); and the clause «فإنهم غير ملومين» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «هم» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The relative noun is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the relative noun in verse (29); the lām in «لأماناتهم» is redundant (zāʾida), and «أماناتهم» is the object of «راعون».

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «بشهاداتهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قائمون».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «على صلاتهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يحافظون».

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: (أولئك في جنات مكرمون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: (فمال الذين كفروا قبلك مهطعين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The fāʾ is resumptive; «ما» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); «قِبَلك», the adverb, is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun; «مهطعين» is a second ḥāl.

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: (عن اليمين وعن الشمال عزين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {مُهْطِعِينَ}; «عِزين» is another ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural.

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يدخل» is accusative by removal of the preposition «في»; «جنة» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «ممَّا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خَلَقْناهم».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The clause «فلا أقسم» is resumptive, and the clause «إنَّا لقادرون» is the answer to the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قادرون»; the preposition and its genitive noun «منهم» is attached to «خيرا»; the clause «وما نحن بمسبوقين» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {إِنَّا لَقَادِرُونَ}; the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ما» acting like ليس.

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: The clause «فذرهم» is resumptive; the clause «يخوضوا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; «يومهم» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the relative noun is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: «يوم» is a badal (substitute) from {يَوْمَهُمُ}; «سراعا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «يخرجون», and the clause «كأنهم يوفضون» is a second ḥāl.

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: «خاشعة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of {يُوفِضُونَ}; «أبصارهم» is the fāʿil of «خاشعة»; the clause «ترهقهم» is a second ḥāl from the fāʿil of {يُوفِضُونَ}; the clause «ذلك اليوم» is resumptive; «الذي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «اليوم».

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (سأل): for whoever drops the hamza, it admits three aspects. The first is that it is from asking (السؤال), but the hamza has been replaced by an alif; this is a replacement not according to analogy, yet it is permissible; Sībawayh and others reported it. The second is that the alif replaces a wāw: Sībawayh and others reported (سلت تسال) as a dialect, on the pattern of (خفت تخاف). The third aspect is that the alif replaces a yāʾ, from (سال يسيل) "to flow", on the pattern of (كال يكيل). The origin of (سأل), when it is from asking, is that it takes two objects, as in His saying (فلا تسألن ما ليس), and it may be limited to one, like (أعطيت) and (كسوت), as in His saying, the Exalted: (واسألوا ما أنفقتم). When you limit it to one, it may pass by a preposition to that one, as in His saying, the Exalted: (سأل سائل بعذاب), its implied form being "An asker asked the Prophet about a punishment", and the bāʾ means (عن). If you make (سال) from flowing (السيل), the bāʾ does not mean (عن) but is in its own proper sense, its origin being for transitivity. As for the hamza in (سائل), it admits three aspects: the first, that it is original, from asking; the second, that it replaces a wāw, according to the dialect of those who say (سلت تسال) like (خفت تخاف); and the third, that it replaces a yāʾ, if you make (سال) from flowing.

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying (يوم تكون السماء): the governor of the adverbial is (نراه). It may also be a badal (substitute) from (قريب), the governor of (قريب) being (نراه). It is also said that the governor is (يبصرونهم). The hāʾ and mīm in (يبصرونهم) refer back to the disbelievers and the nominative pronoun to the believers, i.e. the believers see the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, that is, they see them and look at them in the Fire. It is also said that it refers back to (الحميم), which has a plural meaning, i.e. each close friend sees his close friend. It is also said that both pronouns refer back to the disbelievers, i.e. the followers see those they followed in the Fire.

mekki-muskil:15-16.t: His saying (إنها لظى نزاعة): (لظى) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن), in the position of the nominative, and (نزاعة) is a second khabar. It is also said that (لظى) is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ in (إنها), and (نزاعة) is the khabar, in the position of the nominative. It is also said that (لظى) is the khabar of (إن) and (نزاعة) is a badal from (لظى), or nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). It is also said that the pronoun in (إنها) is the pronoun of the story, (لظى) is a mubtadaʾ, (نزاعة) is the khabar of (لظى), and the clause is the khabar of (إن). Whoever reads (نزاعة) in the accusative takes it as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is the reading of Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim [Translator's note: the printed text has «خفص»; Ḥafṣ is meant]. The governor of (نزاعة) is what the speech indicates of the meaning of blazing, as if He said: "No! It blazes while stripping away the scalps." Al-Mubarrad denied the permissibility of the accusative of (نزاعة) and said: Laẓā is never anything but a stripper of scalps, so there is no sense in a ḥāl; a ḥāl is only for what may be and may not be. This is the meaning of his statement. [Makkī says:] The ḥāl here is permissible because it confirms what precedes it, as He said: (وهو الحق مصدقا), and the truth is never anything but confirming; and the Exalted said: (وهذا صراط ربك مستقيما), and the path of Allah, exalted be His mention, is never anything but straight. So it is not necessary that the ḥāl be only for a thing that may be and may not be; this is a principle that does not hold in every place, so his statement is not good. It has also been said that this is only an announcement to someone who thought that it would not be, so the ḥāl is sound on this view without objection.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying (تدعو من أدبر): a third khabar (predicate) of (إن); or, if you wish, you may cut it off from what precedes it.

mekki-muskil:19-19.t:
His saying (خلق هلوعا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (خلق), and it is the anticipated ḥāl (al-ḥāl al-muqaddara), because anxiety only arises in him after his creation, not at the time of his creation.
His saying (جزوعا) and (منوعا): the khabar (predicate) of an implied (كان), i.e. "he becomes impatient" and "he becomes withholding", or "he turns" and the like. It is also said that it is a naʿt (adjective) of (هلوع), but that is far-fetched, because you would be intending it to come before (إذا).

mekki-muskil:36-36.t: His saying (فمال الذين كفروا): (ما) is an interrogative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (الذين) is the khabar (predicate). (مهطعين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it governs (قبلك); (قبلك) is an adverbial of place.

mekki-muskil:37-37.t: His saying (عزين): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) as well, from (الذين). It is the plural of (عزة). It was pluralised with wāw and nūn, although it is feminine and not rational, so that this would be a compensation for what was deleted from it. It is said that its origin is (عزهة), just as the origin of (سنة) is (سنهة); then the hāʾ was deleted, and its plural with wāw and nūn was made a compensation for the deletion.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t:
His saying (يوم يخرجون): (يوم) is a badal (substitute) from (يومهم), and (يومهم) is accusative governed by (يلاقوا) as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
His saying (سراعا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (يخرجون). Likewise (كأنهم إلى نصب) is also in the position of a ḥāl from the pronoun.

mekki-muskil:44-44.t: His saying (خاشعة): also a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (يخرجون), and likewise (ترهقهم ذلة).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿سأل﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, containing the meaning of دعا (to call for); for that reason it is made transitive the way that verb is made transitive.
﴿سائل﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿بعذاب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سأل﴾.
﴿واقع﴾: a naʿt (adjective), genitive (majrūr).

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿للكافرين﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿واقع﴾.
﴿ليس﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb.
﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of laysa.
﴿دافع﴾: the postponed ism (noun) of laysa; and the clause ﴿ليس له دافع﴾ is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عذاب﴾.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿من الله﴾: من is a preposition and the Name of Majesty is a genitive noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿واقع﴾, or attached to ﴿دافع﴾.
﴿ذي﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ, because it is one of the five nouns.
﴿المعارج﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿تعرج﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; and تعرج is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿الملائكة﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative.
﴿والروح﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الملائكة.
﴿إليه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تعرج﴾.
﴿في يوم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted element indicated by واقع, i.e.: "the punishment will befall them on the Day of Resurrection".
﴿كان﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb.
﴿مقداره﴾: the ism (noun) of kāna, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿خمسين﴾: the khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ, because it is treated like the sound masculine plural.
﴿ألف﴾: tamyīz (specification) of خمسين.
﴿سنة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿فاصبر﴾: the fāʾ of eloquence (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); and اصبر is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).
﴿صبرًا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
﴿جميلا﴾: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿إنهم﴾: inna is an abrogating particle, and ﴿هم﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿يرونه﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause يرونه is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿بعيدًا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because the "seeing" is cognitive (ʿilmiyya); and the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿ونراه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; and ﴿نراه﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif because pronouncing it is impossible; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿قريبًا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi, because the "seeing" is cognitive (ʿilmiyya).

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿يوم﴾: an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قريبًا﴾, or to an omitted element indicated by ﴿واقع﴾, i.e.: "it will befall on the day when … will be".
﴿تكون﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); and the clause ﴿تكون﴾ is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) by the adverb being put in annexation to it.
﴿السماء﴾: the ism (noun) of تكون, nominative.
﴿كالمهل﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل ("like"), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of تكون; and ﴿المهل﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿وتكون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; and ﴿تكون﴾ is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); and the clause ﴿تكون﴾ is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) by conjunction with the preceding clause.
﴿الجبال﴾: the ism (noun) of ﴿تكون﴾, nominative.
﴿كالعهن﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل ("like"), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of ﴿تكون﴾; and ﴿العهن﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is negating.
﴿يسأل﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿حميم﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿حميما﴾: the first object of يسأل, the second object being omitted, its implied form being: "his intercession" and "his help". It has also been said: حميما is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and يسأل has no need of an object.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿يبصرونهم﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is not named (passive), nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the hāʾ is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It has been made transitive to a second object by the doubling (of the middle radical), and the first object has taken the place of the agent. The clause is resumptive with no grammatical position, or a ḥāl (circumstantial), or an attribute (ṣifa), i.e.: "relatives being made to see (them)".
﴿يود﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿المجرم﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿لو يفتدي﴾: لو is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya) in the sense of أن, because it comes after a verb of wishing; together with what falls within its scope it is construed as a maṣdar (verbal noun) which is the object of يودّ, i.e.: "he wishes to ransom (himself)".
﴿من عذاب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يفتدي﴾.
﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and إذٍ: a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) sukūn, because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. The tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, its implied form being: "on the day when the sky will be like molten brass, and the mountains will be like wool, and no intimate friend will ask about an intimate friend".
﴿ببنيه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, likewise attached to ﴿يفتدي﴾.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿وصاحبته﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to بنيه, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra; and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿وأخيه﴾: likewise conjoined, genitive by the yāʾ because it is one of the five nouns; and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿وفصيلته﴾: likewise conjoined (maʿṭūf) to بنيه, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra; and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿التي﴾: a relative noun in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿فصيلته﴾.
﴿تؤويه﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma because of heaviness; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and the clause ﴿تؤويه﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿ومن﴾: likewise conjoined (maʿṭūf); and من is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive.
﴿في الأرض﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause); and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position.
﴿جميعًا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction denoting delay (tarākhī).
﴿ينجيه﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma because of heaviness; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir).

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿إنها﴾: inna is an abrogating particle, and ﴿ها﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿لظى﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿نزاعة﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun concealed in لظى, accusative (manṣūb).
﴿للشوى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نزاعة﴾; genitive (majrūr) by an implied kasra on the alif.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿تدعو﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma because of heaviness; the fāʿil (agent) of تدعو is latent (mustatir), referring to لظى; and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in نزّاعة.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿أدبر﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent; and the clause ﴿أدبر﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
﴿تولى﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أدبر.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿وجمع﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and جمع is a past verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir).
﴿فأوعى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and أوعى is a past verb; its fāʿil is latent.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿الإنسان﴾: the ism (noun) of inna, accusative (manṣūb) by the overt fatḥa; and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿خلق﴾: a past verb whose agent is not named (passive), its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) latent (mustatir); and the clause خلق is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿هلوعا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nāʾib fāʿil, accusative.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb for future time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its response ﴿جزوعًا﴾.
﴿مسه﴾: a past verb, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause مسّه is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) by the adverb being put in annexation to it.
﴿الشر﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿جزوعًا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in ﴿هلوعًا﴾, the implied sense being: "anxious, being impatient at the time evil touches him". It has also been said: it is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿هلوعًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and إذا is an adverb for future time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its response ﴿منوعا﴾.
﴿مسه﴾: a past verb, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause ﴿مسّه﴾ is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) by the adverb being put in annexation to it.
﴿الخير﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿منوعا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in ﴿هلوعا﴾, the implied sense being: "anxious, being withholding at the time good touches him". It has also been said: it is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿هلوعا﴾.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of exception.
﴿المصلين﴾: excepted (mustathnā), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ, because it is a sound masculine plural.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun, a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿المصلين﴾.
﴿هم﴾: an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿على صلاتهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿دائمون﴾.
﴿دائمون﴾: the khabar (predicate) of هم, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw, because it is a sound masculine plural; and the clause ﴿هم على صلاتهم دائمون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿والذين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الذين is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first ﴿الذين﴾, which is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿المصلين﴾.
﴿في أموالهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿حق﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿معلوم﴾: a naʿt, nominative (marfūʿ); and the clause ﴿في أموالهم حق﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿للسائل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second naʿt (adjective) of ﴿حق﴾.
﴿والمحروم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the genitive noun is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to السائل, genitive (majrūr).

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿والذين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الذين is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first ﴿الذين﴾, which is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿المصلين﴾.
﴿يصدقون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause يُصَدِّقُون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿بيوم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يصدقون﴾.
﴿الدين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿والذين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الذين is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first ﴿الذين﴾, which is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿المصلين﴾.
﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿من عذاب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) His saying: ﴿مشفقون﴾.
﴿ربهم﴾: رب is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) and is itself muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿مشفقون﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw; and the clause ﴿هم من عذاب ربهم مشفقون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿عذاب﴾: the ism (noun) of inna, accusative (manṣūb).
﴿ربهم﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿غير﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿مأمون﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿والذين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الذين is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first ﴿الذين﴾, which is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿المصلين﴾.
﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿لفروجهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يحافظون﴾. [Translator's note: the word in this ayah is ﴿حافظون﴾; ﴿يحافظون﴾ belongs to ayah 34 (﴿على صلاتهم يحافظون﴾).]
﴿حافظون﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of exception.
﴿على أزواجهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element which is the excepted (mustathnā), i.e.: "except their guarding them with regard to their wives"; and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿أو﴾: a conjunction.
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of the genitive by conjunction with أزواجهم.
﴿ملكت﴾: a past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; and the clause ﴿ملكت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿أيمانهم﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿فإنهم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; inna is an abrogating particle, and ﴿هم﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿غير﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿ملومين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿فمن﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and من is a conditional noun that puts into the jussive (ism sharṭ jāzim), a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿ابتغى﴾: a past verb in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to من.
﴿وراء﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿ابتغى﴾, for وراء has here left its adverbial use, i.e.: "he sought what is beyond that", i.e. (beyond) enjoyment through marriage and what the right hand possesses. You may also keep it as an adverb and attach it to an omitted attribute (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl bihi, i.e.: "whoever seeks a matter lying beyond that".
