﴿ذلك﴾: a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the verbal clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the conditional noun.
﴿فأولئك﴾: the fāʾ binds the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and أولئك is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ.
﴿هم﴾: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl).
﴿العادون﴾: the khabar of أولئك; and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. Or هم is a second mubtadaʾ and العادون its khabar, and that clause is the khabar of أولئك.

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿والذين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الذين is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first ﴿الذين﴾, which is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿المصلين﴾.
﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿لأماناتهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿راعون﴾; and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿وعهدهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and عهدهم is conjoined to أماناتهم, genitive (majrūr); and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿راعون﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw.

muyesser-irab:33-33.t:
﴿والذين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الذين is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first ﴿الذين﴾, which is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿المصلين﴾.
﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿بشهاداتهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قائمون﴾; and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿قائمون﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t:
﴿والذين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الذين is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first ﴿الذين﴾, which is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿المصلين﴾.
﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿على صلاتهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يحافظون﴾; and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿يحافظون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent); and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t:
﴿أولئك﴾: a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿في جنات﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate), or attached to ﴿مكرمون﴾.
﴿مكرمون﴾: a second khabar.

muyesser-irab:36-36.t:
﴿فمال﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position; ما is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); and the lām is a preposition, indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive; and the preposition and its genitive noun form a quasi-clause (shibh jumla) in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of ما.
﴿كفروا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma; and the wāw is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿قبلك﴾: an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), or to ﴿مهطعين﴾, i.e.: "being in the direction adjoining you, on the right and on the left".
﴿مهطعين﴾: ḥāl from الذين, accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:37-37.t:
﴿عن اليمين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun; it has also been said: attached to ﴿مهطعين﴾.
﴿وعن الشمال﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿عن الشمال﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿عن اليمين﴾.
﴿عزين﴾: likewise a ḥāl from the relative noun, accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ, because it is treated like the sound masculine plural.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t:
﴿أيطمع﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (istifhām inkārī), and يطمع is an imperfect verb.
﴿كل﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿امرئ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿منهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted attribute (ṣifa) of ﴿امرئ﴾.
﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; أن with what falls within its scope is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and the (implied) preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يطمع﴾, i.e.: "does he hope for entering?"
﴿يُدخل﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is not named (passive), in the subjunctive (manṣūb) by ﴿أن﴾; its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿جنة﴾: a second object, by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa).
﴿نعيم﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿إنا﴾: inna is an abrogating particle, and ﴿نا﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿خلقناهم﴾: a past verb; ﴿نا﴾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause خلقناهم is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿مما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلقناهم﴾.
﴿يعلمون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; and the clause يعلمون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:40-40.t:
﴿فلا أقسم برب المشارق والمغارب﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; لا is connective (ṣila); أقسم is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "I" (أنا); and برب المشارق والمغارب is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أقسم﴾.
﴿إنا لقادرون﴾: inna is an abrogating particle and ﴿نا﴾ is its ism (noun); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and قادرون is the khabar (predicate) of inna; and the clause إنّا لقادرون has no grammatical position, because it is the response to the oath.

muyesser-irab:41-41.t:
﴿على﴾: a preposition, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, with no grammatical position.
﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle.
﴿نبدل﴾: an imperfect verb in the subjunctive (manṣūb) by ﴿أن﴾; أن with what falls within its scope is in the position of the genitive by ﴿على﴾, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قادرون﴾.
﴿خيرًا﴾: the object of نبدل.
﴿منهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خيرًا﴾.
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negating mā, which operates like laysa.
﴿نحن﴾: the ism (noun) of ﴿ما﴾.
﴿بمسبوقين﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿مسبوقين﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative in position, genitive in form by the bāʾ.

muyesser-irab:42-42.t:
﴿فذرهم﴾: the fāʾ of eloquence (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); ذرهم: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿يخوضوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn because it is the response to the command; and the wāw is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil.
﴿ويلعبوا﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يخوضوا.
﴿حتى﴾: a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition.
﴿يلاقوا﴾: an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; the wāw is the fāʿil; and the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive by حتى, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) ذرهم.
﴿يومهم﴾: mafʿūl bihi.
﴿الذي﴾: a relative noun, a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿يومهم﴾.
﴿يوعدون﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is not named (passive), nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; and the wāw is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

muyesser-irab:43-43.t:
﴿يوم﴾: يوم is a badal (substitute) of ﴿يومهم﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿يخرجون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn the nūn [Translator's note: the word «النون» is repeated in the source]; the wāw is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent); and the clause يخرجون is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being put in annexation to it.
﴿من الأجداث﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يخرجون﴾.
﴿سراعًا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw, accusative.
﴿كأنهم﴾: kaʾanna is an abrogating particle, and ﴿هم﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿إلى نصب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يوفضون﴾.
﴿يوفضون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil; and the clause يوفضون is the khabar (predicate) of كأنهم; and the clause كأنهم is a second ḥāl, likewise from the wāw, so that the two ḥāls are successive (mutarādifa), or from the pronoun in ﴿سراعًا﴾, so that they are nested (mutadākhila).

muyesser-irab:44-44.t:
﴿خاشعة﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), from the fāʿil (agent) of ﴿يوفضون﴾ or from the fāʿil of ﴿يخرجون﴾; the first is closer.
﴿أبصارهم﴾: the fāʿil of خاشعة, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿ترهقهم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. [Translator's note: so in the source; the hāʾ of ﴿ترهقهم﴾ is in fact the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).]
﴿ذلة﴾: fāʿil, nominative by the ḍamma; and the clause ﴿ترهقهم ذلة﴾ is a second ḥāl, or resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿ذلك﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿اليوم﴾: its khabar (predicate).
﴿الذي﴾: a relative noun in the position of the nominative as an attribute (ṣifa).
﴿كانوا﴾: kāna is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the wāw of the plural is its ism (noun).
﴿يوعدون﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is not named (passive), nominative by the retention of the nūn; and the wāw is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The clause ﴿يوعدون﴾ is the khabar of kāna. The clause ﴿كانوا يوعدون﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. And the clause ﴿ذلك اليوم...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
سَأَلَ سائِلٌ: this is the reading of the people of Kufa and the people of Basra, pronouncing both with hamza. Abū Jaʿfar, al-Aʿraj and Nāfiʿ read سَأَلَ سائِلٌ [i.e. «سالَ سائلٌ»] [Translator's note: the vowelled text reproduces the standard reading, not the variant described]:
the first without hamza and the second with hamza. This reading has two aspects. One of them is that «سال» is from «السيل» (flowing), i.e. it poured down. The other is that «سال» is said in the sense of «سأل», not that it is derived from it [by lightening], because this is not the lightening of the hamza; if it were from it, it could only be by substitution for the hamza, and that is far-fetched and anomalous (shādhdh). Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān hold that it is from the hamzated [root], and that an error was made about it in transmitting from Nāfiʿ, and that he only used to pronounce the hamza between-between (bayna bayna). Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is a far-fetched interpretation and an accusation of error against everyone who transmitted from Nāfiʿ. The right view about it is that Sībawayh reported «سِلْتُ أسالُ» in the sense of «سألتُ» (I asked); so the origin of «سال» is «سَوَل», and when the wāw was vowelled and what preceded it was vowelled, it was turned into an alif — and like it is «خِفْتُ». «سائل» is hamzated in its original form if it is from «سأل»; if it is from «سال», the origin is «ساوِل», on the pattern fāʿil: the wāw was turned into an alif with a quiescent alif before it, and two quiescent letters do not meet, so a hamza was substituted for the alif, as in «صائم» and «خائف». بِعَذابٍ واقِعٍ.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
لِلْكافِرينَ: the view of al-Farrāʾ ]
is that the implied form is "of a punishment for the disbelievers", and in his view «للكافرين» cannot be attached to «واقع». Abū Jaʿfar said: the apparent sense of the Qur'an is otherwise than what he said, and the exegetes are against his view. Mujāhid said: and falling in the Hereafter. Al-Ḥasan said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed:
سَأَلَ سائِلٌ بِعَذابٍ واقِعٍ, and they said: for whom is it, upon whom will it fall? So Allah the Exalted revealed: لِلْكافِرينَ لَيْسَ لَهُ دافِعٌ.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: It has been said: «المعارج» are the steps of Paradise. Ibn [Abī] Najīḥ reported from Mujāhid, who said: the sky.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: «يعرج» [masculine],
treating the plural as masculine. فِي يَوْمٍ كانَ مِقْدارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned several views about it. The highest of what has been said about it is from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: it is the Day of Resurrection; and the meaning is that the measure of Allah's — Mighty and Majestic — reckoning with creation on it, His rewarding them and punishing them, is the measure of fifty thousand years were anyone other than Him the reckoner. This is indicated by the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī: it was said: "O Messenger of Allah, how long this day is!" He said: "For the believer it is lighter than an obligatory prayer that he performs."

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: فَاصْبِرْ: in the face of their harm. صَبْراً جَمِيلًا: with no anxious complaint in it.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: Because they do not believe in it. It has been said: the pronoun in «إنهم» is for the disbelievers and the one in «يرونه» is for the punishment.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: Because it is bound to be, and everything bound to be is near.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: The implied form may be: "this will happen", or "they will see them, on the day the sky is like molten brass". «يوم» was put in construct with the verb because it is in the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), and was conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: The plural of «عِهْنة»; one also says «عُهون».

nahhas-irab:10-11.t:
يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ: there is disagreement among the scholars about this pronoun. From Ibn ʿAbbās: the close friend is shown his close friend, i.e. he sees him and recognizes him, then flees from him. This is one view. Ibn Abī Najīḥ reported from Mujāhid: the believers are shown the disbelievers. And from Ibn Zayd: in the Fire, the followers are shown those they followed. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The most correct of these views is the first, because the close friend has already been mentioned, so for the pronoun to refer back to him is more fitting than for it to refer back to something not mentioned. يَوَدُّ الْمُجْرِمُ لَوْ يَفْتَدِي مِنْ عَذابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ بِبَنِيهِ:
«يومئذ» was made indeclinable »
because it was put in construct with something not inflected; if you wish, you put it in the genitive by the construct, and read مِنْ عَذابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ بِبَنِيهِ [i.e. «يومئذٍ»].

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: That is, then the ransoming would save him, because يَفْتَدِي indicates ransoming.

nahhas-irab:15-16.t:
كَلَّا: a good stopping point. إِنَّها لَظى نَزَّاعَةً لِلشَّوى: there is disagreement among the grammarians about this. «لظى» may be in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from your saying «ها», with «نزّاعة» the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ». It has been said: لَظى is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «إن», and نَزَّاعَةً is a second khabar, or a badal, or [nominative] by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). And it has been said: «ها» is an allusion (kināya) to the story [i.e. the pronoun of the matter], and لَظى نَزَّاعَةً are a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, and together they are the khabar of «إنّ». Abū ʿUbayd permitted نَزَّاعَةً
in the accusative, and reported that it was not read so. Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd does not permit the accusative here, because it cannot be anything but "stripping off the scalp", and that is not how a ḥāl (circumstantial) behaves.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: Figurative (majāz), because it is reported that its keepers call out: "Bring us whoever turned away and turned his back on obeying Allah." Saʿīd reported from Qatāda: it calls whoever turned away from obeying Allah and turned his back on His Book and His right.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: That is, he put the wealth in a container and did not pay the dues from it. One says «وعيتُ العلم» (I retained the knowledge) and «أوعيتُ المتاع» (I put the goods in a container).

nahhas-irab:19-21.t: إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً (19) إِذا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ جَزُوعاً (20) وَإِذا مَسَّهُ الْخَيْرُ مَنُوعاً (21): خُلِقَ is in the position of the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ», and you put هَلُوعاً in the accusative as an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial) (ḥāl muqaddara). «الهلوع», according to what the lexicographers report, is one who, in a state of poverty, shows what he should not show of anxious complaint and lack of fortitude, and in wealth shows what he should not show of withholding the obligatory due and lack of gratitude. He has explained this by His saying: إِذا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ جَزُوعاً وَإِذا مَسَّهُ الْخَيْرُ مَنُوعاً. You put جَزُوعاً and مَنُوعاً in the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «هلوع»; the implied form may also be "he became such".

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: Conjoined to it. Saʿīd reported that Qatāda said: the obligatory charity (zakat). Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: وَالَّذِينَ فِي أَمْوالِهِمْ حَقٌّ مَعْلُومٌ: he said: He means apart from the charity, by which he maintains ties of kinship, strengthens a weak person, bears the burden of a dependant, or helps a deprived person.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: it is soundly reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: «المحروم» is the one denied the means of livelihood. From Qatāda: «السائل» is the one who begs with his palm, and «المحروم» is the one who refrains, i.e. who does not beg; and each has a right over you, O son of Adam. From Ibn Zayd: «المحروم» is the one whose crops have burned.

nahhas-irab:26-34.t:
فَمَنِ ابْتَغى وَراءَ ذلِكَ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ العادُونَ (31) وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَماناتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ راعُونَ (32) وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ بِشَهاداتِهِمْ قائِمُونَ (33) وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ يُحافِظُونَ (34)
وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ مِنْ عَذابِ رَبِّهِمْ مُشْفِقُونَ: in the position of the accusative; all of it is conjoined to the naʿt (adjective) of «المصلّين», and likewise وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حافِظُونَ, and likewise وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ بِشَهاداتِهِمْ قائِمُونَ. Abū Jaʿfar said: the reading of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and al-Ḥasan is بِشَهاداتِهِمْ [Translator's note: the vowelled text shows the plural; the variant ascribed to them is evidently the singular «بشهاداتهم», as the following explanation shows].
Abū Jaʿfar said: «شهادة» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), so for that reason a group read it in the singular; it may also be a singular indicating a plural. Likewise وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ يُحافِظُونَ.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: Accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ الشِّمالِ عِزِينَ: the plural of «عِزَة», pluralized with wāw and nūn although it contains the sign of the feminine, [the plural] being compensation for what was dropped from it. There is another dialect form: one says «مررتُ بقومٍ عِزينٍ», placing the inflection on the nūn.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t:
The reading of al-Ḥasan and Ṭalḥa is أَنْ يُدْخَلَ [i.e. «أن يدخل»]
with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the khāʾ. [Translator's note: the vowelled text reproduces the standard reading, not the variant described.] Abū Jaʿfar said:
The verse is difficult. Among what has been said about it is that the meaning is: what is the matter with those who disbelieve, hastening towards you with denial of you? And it has been said: [hastening] to listen to you so as to find fault with you. عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ الشِّمالِ عِزِينَ: that is, divided in their religions while opposing Islam — does every man of them hope to be rewarded for this and enter Paradise? And it has been said:
does every man of them hope to be saved from the punishment despite this deed? — because the meaning of "entering Paradise" is being saved from the punishment.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: كَلَّا: a rebuttal of them. إِنَّا خَلَقْناهُمْ مِمَّا يَعْلَمُونَ: He reminded them of their lowliness, and that they were created only from a drop of fluid; so how would they deserve reward if they have not done righteous deeds? As Qatāda said: you were created from filth, O son of Adam, so fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ الْمَشارِقِ وَالْمَغارِبِ: Abū Ẓabyān said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: the sun has every day a place of rising and a place of setting that it did not have the day before; and that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ الْمَشارِقِ وَالْمَغارِبِ. «لا» is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis; we know of no disagreement about that. They only disagreed about «لا أقسم» [in Sūrat al-Qiyāma] because it is the beginning of the sūra, and they disliked saying "redundant at the beginning of the sūra"; the grammarians agree that «لا» and «ما» are not added redundantly at the beginning of speech, so the discussion there was more difficult. The answer to the oath is: إِنَّا لَقادِرُونَ.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: That is, they cannot frustrate Us or escape Us, because whoever has a thing escape him and does not catch up with it has been outstripped by it.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُوا وَيَلْعَبُوا: an answer (jawāb), carrying the sense of a condition; whereas in another place ثُمَّ ذَرْهُمْ فِي خَوْضِهِمْ يَلْعَبُونَ [al-Anʿām: 91], because that is not an answer. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd claimed that the difference between them is that when it is with the nūn, they are in that state [at the time], and when it is without the nūn, it is for the future. يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ: a badal (substitute) from it. مِنَ الْأَجْداثِ سِراعاً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلى نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ: the reading of al-Ḥasan is إِلى نُصُبٍ [i.e. «نَصْبٍ»] [Translator's note: the vowelled text reproduces the standard reading, not the variant described],
and likewise it is reported from Zayd ibn Thābit and Abū al-ʿĀliya: that is, racing towards goals. Al-Ḥasan said: they used to gather in the early morning and sit, and when the sun rose they would rush to their idols (anṣāb). Al-Aʿraj said: «إلى نَصْبٍ» means to a banner. Abū Jaʿfar said: its implied form in Arabic is "to a banner that has been set up (nuṣiba naṣban)".

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
خاشِعَةً أَبْصارُهُمْ: that is, humbled and submissive because of what has befallen them. «خاشعةً» is accusative by «ترهقهم» or by «يخرجون». تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ: that is, covers them. ذلِكَ الْيَوْمُ الَّذِي كانُوا يُوعَدُونَ:
It has been said: [the day] which the polytheists of Quraysh were promised, and they did not believe it. [Translator's note: the text reads «الذي كانوا مشركو قريش يوعدون به», with a grammatical irregularity in «كانوا مشركو».]

safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(بعذاب) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (سأل) [Note: Either the bāʾ has the meaning of عن, or the verb سأل is made to include the meaning of دعا.], (للكافرين) attached to (واقع) [Note: The lām is causal, i.e. for the sake of the disbelievers, or it has the meaning of على; it is also permissible to attach the preposition phrase to (سأل) by making it include the meaning of دعا.], (له) attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of ليس; (من الله) attached to (واقع) [Note: Or attached to دافع.] (إليه) attached to (تعرج), (في يوم) attached to (تعرج) [Note: Or attached to an omitted verb indicated by واقع, i.e. "the punishment occurs on a day..".], (ألف) tamyīz (specification) of the number خمسين; (سنة) muḍāf ilayhi — tamyīz of the number ألف — genitive (majrūr).
The clause «سأل سائل ...» has no grammatical position: initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «ليس له دافع» is in the position of a genitive, naʿt (adjective) of عذاب. The clause «تعرج الملائكة ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كان مقداره خمسين ...» is in the position of a genitive, naʿt of يوم.

* Morphology:
(خمسين): a noun for the number, one of the words for the decades, treated like the sound masculine plural; its pattern is فعلين, with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
The art of representation (tamthīl): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «تَعْرُجُ الْمَلائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ إِلَيْهِ فِي يَوْمٍ كانَ مِقْدارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ». It is an allusion to the lengthiness of that day because of its severity, not that it is literally of this numerical measure. The Arabs describe times of hardship and grief as long, and times of ease and relief as short. It has also been said: the speech is an explanation of the utmost height of those ascending ways and the remoteness of their extent, by way of representation and imaginative depiction.

safi-cedvel:5-10.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking to the answer of an implied condition; (بعيدا) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, its governor being يرونه; (قريبا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, its governor being نراه; (يوم) adverb of time, accusative, badal (substitute) of (قريبا) [Note: Or attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "the punishment occurs" ... And if the pronoun in (نراه) refers to the Day of Resurrection, the adverb is a badal of the pronoun.], (المهل) attached to the khabar (predicate) of the first تكون; (كالعهن) attached to the khabar of the second تكون; (الواو) conjunction; (حميما) mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: Or accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. «عن حميم».], the second object being implied (muqaddar), i.e. his help or his support.
The clause «اصبر ...» is in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the answer of an implied condition, i.e. "if a questioner asks, then be patient ...".
The clause «إنّهم يرونه ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī). The clause «يرونه ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of إنّ.
The clause «نراه ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّهم يرونه. The clause «تكون السماء ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تكون الجبال ...» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause تكون السماء.
The clause «يسأل حميم ...» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause تكون السماء ...

* Morphology:
(العهن): a noun for wool, or for the red kind of it; its pattern is فعل, with kasra then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
The unqualified simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «يَوْمَ تَكُونُ السَّماءُ كَالْمُهْلِ».
This is an unqualified simile, and the point of resemblance is the changing of colours, i.e. like molten silver in its changing colours.
Then in the following verse comes «وَتَكُونُ الْجِبالُ كَالْعِهْنِ», and the point of resemblance is the flying about and scattering.
What is meant is that they are like wool dyed in various colours, because the mountains have streaks, white and red, of differing colours, and jet-black. So when they are crumbled and sent flying in the air, they resemble carded wool when the wind sends it flying.

safi-cedvel:11-14.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) in يبصّرونهم is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (لو) a maṣdar particle; (من عذاب) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يفتدي) ...
The interpreted maṣdar (لو يفتدي ...) is in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being يودّ.
(يومئذ) an adverb annexed to an adverb, and the first is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive [Translator's note: so in the source; the first element يوم is the muḍāf and إذ the muḍāf ilayhi.]; (ببنيه) attached to (يفتدي), (الواو) conjunction in the four places; (التي) relative noun in the position of a genitive, naʿt (adjective) of فصيلته; (في الأرض) attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of من; (جميعا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the implied returning pronoun in the ṣila; (ثمّ) conjunction ...
The clause «يبصّرونهم ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يودّ المجرم ...» has no grammatical position: another explanatory resumption [Note: Or in the position of an accusative, ḥāl of the deputy agent of (يبصّرونهم) or of its object, with the linking pronoun implied, i.e. "the criminal among them wishes".].
The clause «يفتدي ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle-relative (لو).
The clause «تؤويه ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative (التي).
The clause «ينجيه ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause of the particle-relative.

* Morphology:
(13) فصيلة: a noun for the clan; its pattern is فعيلة with the meaning of مفعولة, derived from الفصل (separating).
(تؤويه): imperfect of آوى; in it the added hamza is dropped for lightness, by analogy with (يؤمن) — see verse (3) of Sūrat al-Baqara — its pattern is تفعله ... The yāʾ has undergone iʿlāl (phonological change) by being made quiescent, because of the heaviness of the vowel.
(14) ينجيه: imperfect of أنجى; in it the added hamza is dropped; its case is the same as تؤويه above, and likewise the iʿlāl.

safi-cedvel:15-18.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) a particle of rebuff and rebuke for what the criminal wishes; (نزّاعة) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the pronoun in لظى; (للشوى) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نزّاعة) [Note: Or the lām is redundant, for strengthening, and الشوى is genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of نزّاعة.], (الواو) conjunction, and likewise (الفاء) ..
The clause «إنّها لظى ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تدعو ...» is in the position of a nominative, a second khabar (predicate) of (إنّ) [Note: Or a ḥāl of the pronoun in نزّاعة.].
The clause «أدبر ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «تولّى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أدبر.
The clause «جمع ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أدبر.
The clause «أوعى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause جمع.

* Morphology:
(لظى): a noun for flame, then used as a proper name for Hell, so it is denied tanwīn (a diptote) because of being a proper name and feminine; its pattern is فعل, with two fatḥas.
(نزّاعة): intensive form of the active participle from the transitive triliteral نزع; its pattern is فعّالة, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and shadda on the ʿayn.
(الشوى): plural of شواة, which is the skin of the head, or the extremity, or the limb that is not a fatal spot, or it is the skin of a human being. The pattern of شواة is فعلة with two fatḥas, and in it there is iʿlāl (phonological change) by substitution: its origin is شوي — with a yāʾ at its end; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was changed to alif. Likewise in شواة, whose origin is شوية with three fatḥas.
(أوعى): in it there is iʿlāl by substitution; its origin is أوعي; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was changed to alif; its pattern is أفعل.

* Rhetoric:
Metaphor (istiʿāra): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «تَدْعُوا مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّى».
Here its suitability for them — or, as has been said, their deserving it — is likened to its calling them. So that was expressed by "calling", by way of metaphor. It has also been said: تدعو means "it destroys", from the Arabs' saying دعاك الله, i.e. "may Allah destroy you". Of this is the poet's saying:
دعاك الله من رجل بأفعى ... إذا نام العيون سرت عليكا
(May Allah destroy you, what a man, by a viper that creeps upon you when eyes sleep.)

safi-cedvel:19-35.t:
* I'rab:
(هلوعا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: It is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), since man is not characterised by it at the time of his creation.], (إذا) adverb for the future, including the meaning of condition [Note: Or not including the meaning of condition, in which case it is attached to (جزوعا); the same is said of the second (إذا), and it is attached to (منوعا).], in the position of an accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the content of the implied apodosis; (جزوعا) khabar (predicate) of an implied كان — or صار; (الواو) conjunction; (إذا مسّه الخير منوعا) like إذا مسّه الشرّ جزوعا; (إلّا) for exception; (المصلّين) excepted by إلّا from الإنسان, which denotes the genus; accusative ...
The clause «إنّ الإنسان ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «خلق هلوعا ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of إنّ.
The clause «مسّه الشرّ ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «(كان) جزوعا ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussivising condition.
The clause «مسّه الخير ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «(كان) منوعا ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussivising condition.
23-28 (الذين) relative noun in the position of an accusative, naʿt (adjective) of المصلّين; (على صلاتهم) attached to (دائمون), the khabar; (في أموالهم) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (حقّ); (للسائل) attached to a second naʿt of (حقّ); (بيوم) attached to (يصدّقون); (من عذاب) attached to the khabar (مشفقون) ...
The clause «هم ... دائمون» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative (الذين).
The clause «في أموالهم حقّ ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «يصدّقون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the third relative (الذين).
The clause «هم ... مشفقون» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the fourth relative (الذين).
The clause «إنّ عذاب ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
29-30 (الواو) conjunction; (الذين) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the previous relative, in the position of an accusative; (لفروجهم) attached to (حافظون); (إلّا) for exception; (على أزواجهم) attached to an omitted element, which is the excepted [Note: I.e. "except guarding them with respect to their wives".]; (أو) conjunction; (ما) relative noun in the position of a genitive, conjoined to أزواجهم; (الفاء) causal [Note: Or linking to the answer of an implied condition.] ...
The clause «هم ... حافظون» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the fifth relative (الذين).
The clause «ملكت أيمانهم ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «إنّهم غير ملومين ...» has no grammatical position: causal [Note: Or it is the answer of an implied condition, i.e. "if they do not guard them except with respect to their wives, then they ..."].
31- (الفاء) resumptive; (من) jussivising conditional noun in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ; (وراء) adverb of place, accusative, attached to a naʿt of the implied object of ابتغى, i.e. "seeks a matter that lies beyond that"; (الفاء) linking to the answer of the stated condition; (هم) separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is العادون, and the nominal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.].
The clause «من ابتغى ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ابتغى ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of condition and answer together.].
The clause «أولئك ... العادون» is in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the answer of the stated condition, joined with the fāʾ.
32-35 (الواو) conjunction; (الذين) conjoined to the first relative, in the position of an accusative; (لأماناتهم) attached to (راعون); (بشهادتهم) attached to (قائمون); (على صلاتهم) attached to (يحافظون); (في جنّات) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك) [Note: Or attached to (مكرمون).] (مكرمون) a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك), nominative ...
The clause «هم ... راعون» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the sixth relative (الذين).
The clause «هم ... قائمون» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the seventh relative (الذين).
The clause «يحافظون ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
The clause «هم ... يحافظون» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the eighth relative (الذين).
The clause «أولئك في جنّات ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

* Morphology:
(19) هلوعا: ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from the triliteral هلع, of the class of فرح, meaning intense anxiety and lack of patience in misfortunes; it may also be an intensive form of the active participle.
(20) جزوعا: ṣifa mushabbaha from the triliteral جزع, of the class of فرح, meaning "to be alarmed at something"; its pattern is فعول, and it may be an intensive form of the active participle.
(21) منوعا: an intensive form from the triliteral منع, of the class of فتح; its pattern is فعول, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(22) المصلّين: plural of المصلّي, active participle from the quadriliteral صلّى; its pattern is مفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the doubled ʿayn ... In المصلّين there is iʿlāl (phonological change) by deletion because of the meeting of two quiescents; its origin is المصلّيين with two yāʾs.
(28) مأمون: passive participle from the triliteral أمن; its pattern is مفعول.
(31) ملومين: plural of ملوم, passive participle from the triliteral لام; it is on the pattern مقول, with the wāw of مفعول deleted. Its origin is ملووم; the wāw, the ʿayn of the word, was made quiescent and its vowel transferred to the letter before it, then the wāw of مفعول was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescents. [Translator's note: ملومين occurs in verse 30 in the standard numbering, and ابتغى below in verse 31; the source numbers them (31) and (32).]
(32) ابتغى: in it there is iʿlāl by substitution; its origin is ابتغي — with a yāʾ at its end — the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was changed to alif.

* Rhetoric:
Repetition (takrīr): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ يُحافِظُونَ».
The prayer is repeated and they are described by it first and last under two considerations: to indicate its excellence and its precedence over all other acts of obedience. The relatives are repeated in order to treat the difference of attributes as though it were a difference of persons. It has also been said: what is meant is that they observe its conditions and complete its obligatory parts, its sunnas and its recommended parts, by metaphorically borrowing "guarding from loss" for completing and perfecting.

* Benefits:
Guarding the prayer:
Allah described the believers as constant and persevering in prayer — in a previous verse — and described them — in this verse — as guarding it, i.e. performing it completely, with its pillars and conditions. Many ḥadīths and verses have come concerning prayer:
From Jābir — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: «Between a man and polytheism and disbelief is the abandoning of prayer.» Narrated by Muslim.
From Abū Hurayra — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: The first of his deeds for which the servant will be brought to account on the Day of Resurrection is his prayer. If it is sound, he has prospered and succeeded; and if it is corrupt, he has failed and lost. If anything is lacking from his obligatory prayer, the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: Look whether My servant has any voluntary prayer, so that what is lacking of the obligatory may be completed by it? Then the rest of his deeds will be treated in this way. Narrated by al-Tirmidhī, who said: a ḥasan ḥadīth.
From ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: «There is no Muslim man whom a prescribed prayer comes upon, and he perfects its ablution, its humility and its bowing, but that it is an expiation for the sins before it, so long as a major sin is not committed; and that is for all time.» Narrated by Muslim.

safi-cedvel:36-39.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (ما) interrogative noun in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (للذين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ما; (قبلك) adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the relative; (مهطعين) a second ḥāl of the relative, accusative; (عن اليمين) attached to (عزين) «1», and likewise (عن الشمال) «2»; (عزين) another ḥāl of the relative [Note: Or a ḥāl of the pronoun in (مهطعين), making it an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila).].
The clause «ما للذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
38- (الهمزة) for rhetorical (disapproving) interrogation; (منهم) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of كلّ امرئ; (أن) maṣdar and subjunctive particle ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يدخل) is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (يطمع), i.e. «في أن يدخل».
The clause «يطمع كلّ امرئ ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يدخل ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
39- (كلّا) a particle of rebuff and rebuke; (ممّا) attached to (خلقناهم) ..
The clause «إنّا خلقناهم ...» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «خلقناهم ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of إنّ.
The clause «يعلمون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(36) قبلك: an adverbial noun meaning direction; its pattern is فعل, with kasra then fatḥa ... It may also come with the meaning of capacity [Note: See verse (37) of Sūrat al-Naml.].
(37) عزين: plural of عزة, meaning a group, and it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ). It has been said that the hāʾ has been deleted from it, its origin being عزهة ... It has been said that its final radical (lām) is wāw, from عزوته أعزوه, i.e. "I traced his lineage". And it has been said that its lām is yāʾ, i.e. عزيته أعزيه, with the meaning of عزوته.. It has been treated like the sound masculine plural because its lām was deleted, and it may take a broken plural, عزى, on the pattern فعل with kasra then fatḥa ... Al-Aṣmaʿī said: العزون are the classes (groups).

safi-cedvel:40-41.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (لا أقسم) its i'rab has preceded [Note: In verse (38) of the preceding Sūrat al-Ḥāqqa.], (بربّ) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أقسم), (اللام) for emphasis, in the position of the lām of the oath; (أن) maṣdar and subjunctive particle; (خيرا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, and it is the adjective of an omitted qualified noun; (منهم) attached to (خيرا); (الواو) conjunction; (ما) negative, operating like laysa; (مسبوقين) genitive in form, accusative in position, khabar (predicate) of ما ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نبدّل ...) is in the position of a genitive by (على), attached to (قادرون).
The clause «أقسم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّا لقادرون» has no grammatical position: the answer of the oath.
The clause «نبدّل ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «ما نحن بمسبوقين» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the answer of the oath.

safi-cedvel:42-44.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking to the answer of an implied condition; (يخوضوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), answer of the imperative; (حتّى) particle of limit and of the genitive; (يلاقوا) imperfect verb, subjunctive by an implied أن after حتّى; (يومهم) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الذي) relative noun in the position of an accusative, naʿt (adjective) of (يومهم); and (الواو) in (يوعدون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يلاقوا ...) is in the position of a genitive by (حتّى), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يخوضوا، ويلعبوا).
The clause «ذرهم ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of an implied condition, i.e. "if it becomes clear that We have power over them, then leave them ...".
The clause «... يخوضوا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of another implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ, i.e. "if you leave them, they will plunge into it".
The clause «يلعبوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يخوضوا.
The clause «يلاقوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يوعدون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative (الذي).
43- (يوم) badal (substitute) of يومهم, accusative; (من الأجداث) attached to (يخرجون), (سراعا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the agent of يخرجون; (إلى نصب) attached to (يوفضون) ..
The clause «يخرجون ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «كأنّهم ... يوفضون» is in the position of an accusative, ḥāl of the agent of يخرجون, or of the pronoun in (سراعا).
The clause «يوفضون» is in the position of a nominative, khabar (predicate) of كأنّ.
44- (خاشعة) ḥāl of the agent of يوفضون; (أبصارهم) fāʿil (agent) of the active participle خاشعة, nominative; the demonstrative points to the punishment about which they asked at the beginning of the sūra; (اليوم) khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: It is permissible for (اليوم) to be a badal of the demonstrative — or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it — and (الذي) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ... The demonstrative then points to the day mentioned earlier in His saying: (يومهم الذي يوعدون).], and this is with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the punishment of the day which ..."; (الذي) relative noun in the position of a nominative, naʿt of اليوم; and (الواو) in (يوعدون) is the deputy agent.
The clause «ترهقهم ذلّة ...» is in the position of an accusative, ḥāl of the agent of يوفضون [Note: It may be cut off as a resumption, and so have no grammatical position.].
The clause «ذلك اليوم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كانوا يوعدون» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «يوعدون ...» is in the position of an accusative, khabar of كانوا.

* Benefits:
- حتى that enters upon the subjunctive imperfect has three meanings:
1- Synonymous with (إلى) "until", as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «قالُوا لَنْ نَبْرَحَ عَلَيْهِ عاكِفِينَ حَتَّى يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْنا مُوسى».
2- Synonymous with causal (كي) "so that", as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وَلا يَزالُونَ يُقاتِلُونَكُمْ حَتَّى يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَنْ دِينِكُمْ» (هُمُ الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ لا تُنْفِقُوا عَلى مَنْ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ حَتَّى يَنْفَضُّوا).
3- And synonymous with إلا in exception. This meaning is apparent from Sībawayh's statement in explaining their saying «والله لا أفعل إلا أن تفعل» (By Allah, I will not do it unless you do): the meaning is «حتى أن تفعل» ... Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted it from some of them regarding the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَما يُعَلِّمانِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ حَتَّى يَقُولا إِنَّما نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌ فَلا تَكْفُرْ». This meaning is apparent in what Ibn Mālik recited from al-Muqannaʿ al-Kindī:
ليس العطاء من الفضول سماحة ... حتى تجود وما لديك قليل
(Giving from surplus is not generosity, unless you give when what you have is little.)
The verb after حتى is not made subjunctive unless it is future. Then, if its futurity is with respect to the time of speaking, the subjunctive is obligatory; and if it is only relative to what precedes it, both options are permissible, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَزُلْزِلُوا حَتَّى يَقُولَ الرَّسُولُ»: their saying is future with respect to the shaking, not with respect to the time when that was narrated to us.
Likewise, the verb after حتى is not made nominative (indicative) unless it is present. Then, if its being present is relative to the time of speaking, the nominative is obligatory, as in your saying «سرت حتى أدخلها» (I travelled until I am entering it), if you say that while you are in the act of entering. Know that the verb after حتى is not made nominative except under three conditions:
1- That it be present, or interpreted as present, as has passed.
2- That it be caused by what precedes it; so «سرت حتى تطلع الشمس» is not permissible, because the rising of the sun is not caused by the travelling.
3- That it be a complement (faḍla); so «سيري حتى أدخلها» is not correct, lest the mubtadaʾ remain without a khabar.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {سَأَلَ}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with a pure alif (سَالَ), and the rest with a fully pronounced hamza, which is the original form and the widespread usage. Then for «سأل» you have two views. First: that it has been made to include the meaning of «دعا» (to call for), which is why it is made transitive with the bāʾ, as you say «دعوت بكذا» ("I called for such-and-such"); the meaning is "a caller called for a punishment." Second: that it keeps its original meaning, and the bāʾ means «عن» (about), as in his saying:
4326 - فإن تَسْألوني بالنساء. . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
«فأسْأل بن خبيرا»
(If you ask me about women, ask one who is well informed.) The matter has been examined before. The first is preferable, because figurative extension in the verb is preferable to that in the particle, because of the verb's strength.
As for the reading with the alif, it has three views. First: that it has the same meaning as the reading with the hamza, and it was lightened by turning the hamza into an alif; this is not the regular way of lightening such a hamza, since the regular way to lighten it is to make it between the two (بينَ بينَ). On this view the bāʾ is as in the view given above. Second: that it comes from «سال يَسال» like «خاف يَخاف», the middle radical being wāw. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the dialect of Quraysh; they say «سِلْتَ تَسالُ», and «هما يتسايلان»." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "One should verify his statement that it is the dialect of Quraysh, because whatever occurs in the Qur'an from the root of asking is hamzated, or its origin is hamzated, as in the reading of the one who read «وسَلُوا اللهُ مِنْ فضلِه» [al-Nisāʾ: 32]. It cannot be from «سال» with wāw as the middle radical, for then it would be «وسَالوا اللهَ», like «خافوا». It is improbable that all of that would come in a dialect other than Quraysh, whose language the Qur'an was revealed in, except for a small part in which the dialect of others occurs. Then in al-Zamakhsharī's words «وهما يتسايَلان» is spelled with yāʾ, which is a slip of the copyists; the correct form is «يتساوَلان» with wāw, because he stated explicitly at the start that it is from السُوال, meaning with a clear wāw, and Abū Zayd has related from the Arabs: «هما يتساولان»." Third: that it comes from السَّيَلان (flowing), the meaning being: "a valley in Hell flowed with punishment," so the middle radical is yāʾ. This is supported by the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās «سالَ سَيْلٌ». al-Zamakhsharī said: "السَّيْل is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of السائل (the flowing one), like الغَوْر in the sense of الغائر. The meaning is: a valley of punishment rushed upon them." End of quotation. The apparent view is the first, because that is established as a well-known dialect. The poet said:
4327 - سالَتْ هُذَيْلٌ رسولَ اللهِ فاحشةً ... ضَلَّتْ هُذَيلٌ بما سالَتْ ولم تُصِبِ
(Hudhayl asked the Messenger of Allah for an indecency; Hudhayl went astray by what it asked and did not hit the mark.) Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh read «سال سالٌ», like «مال». Its explanation is that the original is «سائلٌ», and the middle radical, which is the hamza, was dropped, with the lām (final radical) as the place of the case ending. This is as it was said «هذا شاكٌ» for «شائِكِ السِّلاح» (bristling with weapons). The discussion of the root of asking has already been given at the beginning of al-Baqara; so consult it.
The bāʾ is attached to «سال» from السَّيَلان in the way it is attached in «سال الماءُ بزيدٍ» ("the water flowed with Zayd"). Some made the bāʾ attached to a maṣdar that the verb of asking points to, as if it were said: "What is their asking?" and it was said: "Their asking is for a punishment." Thus the Shaykh related from the Imam Fakhr al-Dīn and did not object. This is strange, for his first statement that it is "attached to a maṣdar that the verb of asking points to" contradicts his implied form «سؤالُهم بعذاب»; for in this implied construction the bāʾ is attached to an omitted element, because it is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), and not to the asking (السؤال).
al-Zamakhsharī said: "On the authority of Qatāda: someone asked about the punishment of Allah, for whom it would descend and upon whom it would fall; so this was revealed. On this view «سأَل» is made to include the meaning of «عُنِيَ» (was concerned) and «اهتمّ» (took an interest)."

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {لِلْكَافِرِينَ}: There are several views. First: that it is attached to «سأل», which includes the meaning of «دعا» as above, that is: "He called for an impending punishment for them." Second: that it is attached to «واقعٍ», the lām expressing cause, that is: "descending on account of them." Third: that it is attached to an omitted element as a second ṣifa (adjective) of «عذابٍ», that is: "existing for the unbelievers." Fourth: that it is an answer to the asker, so it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "it is for the unbelievers." Fifth: that the lām means «على» (upon), that is: "falling upon the unbelievers." This is supported by Ubayy's reading «على الكافرين». On this view it is attached to «واقعٍ», unlike the view stated just before it.
al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: to what is His saying «للكافرين» connected? I say: on the first view it is connected to عذاب as an adjective of it, that is: 'a punishment that is impending, existing for the unbelievers'; or to the verb, that is: 'he called, for the unbelievers, for an impending punishment'; or to واقع, that is: 'a punishment descending on account of them.' On the second view it is a fresh sentence, an answer to the asker, that is: 'it is for the unbelievers.'" End of quotation.
The Shaykh said: "al-Zamakhsharī said: 'or to the verb, that is: he called for the unbelievers'; then he said: 'and on the second,' which is the second of what he mentioned in his explanation of للكافرين, he said: 'it is a fresh sentence, an answer to the asker, that is: it is for the unbelievers.' He had established that «سَأَلَ» includes the meaning of «دعا» and so is made transitive like it, as if he had said: 'a caller called for a punishment,' from your saying «دعا بكذا» when one summons and requests it; from this is His saying, the Exalted: {يَدْعُونَ فِيهَا بِكلِّ فَاكِهَةٍ} [al-Dukhān: 55]." End of quotation. "According to what he established, that it is attached to «دعا», meaning to «سأل», how can it be a fresh sentence, an answer to the asker, that is: it is for the unbelievers? This is not correct."
This is the Shaykh's statement in full. He erred in understanding from Abū al-Qāsim his words «وعلى الثاني إلى آخره» ("and on the second, and so on"); from there came the confusion he mentioned. What al-Zamakhsharī meant by "the second" is his saying: "On the authority of Qatāda: someone asked about the punishment of Allah, upon whom it would descend and for whom it would fall, so it was revealed, and «سأَلَ» on this view includes the meaning of «عُنِيَ» and «اهتم»." This is the second view, which is the counterpart of the first view, namely that «سأَلَ» includes the meaning of «دعا». I do not know how the Shaykh became so confused as to fall into what he fell into, and ascribe error to al-Zamakhsharī, and say that he took the statement of Qatāda and al-Ḥasan and corrupted it. The order in which al-Zamakhsharī arranged the attachment of the lām is among the best there could be, in craft and in meaning.
His saying: {لَيْسَ لهُ دافِعٌ}: It is permissible that it be another naʿt (adjective) of «عذابٍ», or that it be a fresh sentence, the first being more apparent; or that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «عذاب» because it has been specified, either by the action or by the adjective; or that it be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «للكافرين» if we make it an adjective of «عذابٍ».

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {مِّنَ الله}: It is permissible that it be attached to «دافعٌ», meaning: "it has no repeller from Him when its time comes"; or attached to «واقع», and with this al-Zamakhsharī began, that is: "impending from Him." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The negation does not prevent that, because «ليس» is a verb." It is as though he sensed that what precedes a negation does not govern what follows it, so he answered that since the negation here is a verb, that is allowed.
The Shaykh said: "The better view is that «من الله» is attached to «واقعٍ», and «ليس له دافعٌ» is a parenthetical clause (jumla iʿtirāḍiyya) between the governing word and what it governs." End of quotation. This holds only on the view that the clause is a fresh sentence and not an adjective of «عذاب», and that is not the apparent view, as already stated, since parts of the discourse are bound to one another.
His saying: {ذِي}: It is an adjective of «الله». The majority read «تَعْرُج» with tāʾ (two dots above), and al-Kisāʾī read it with yāʾ (two dots below); both are like the two readings of «فناداه الملائكةُ», with the tāʾ. Some considered it weak, because the point of articulation of the jīm is far from that of the tāʾ. The answer was given that it is close to the shīn, because the breath in the shīn brings it near the point of articulation of the tāʾ; and the jīm is assimilated into the shīn because of the closeness between them in point of articulation and quality, as already discussed under {أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ} [al-Fatḥ: 29]. So the assimilation into the tāʾ was carried over from the assimilation into the shīn, because of the closeness between the shīn and the tāʾ. It was also answered that assimilation occurs by sharing qualities alone, even if the two letters are not close in point of articulation, and the jīm shares with the tāʾ the qualities of lowness (istifāl), openness (infitāḥ) and stoppage (shidda). The discussion of «المعارج» has been given in al-Zukhruf.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {والروح}: This is an instance of conjoining the particular to the general (ʿaṭf al-khāṣṣ ʿalā al-ʿāmm), if by الروح is meant Gabriel, peace be upon him, or another angel of their kind. It is placed later here, and placed earlier in His saying: {يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الروح والملائكة صَفّاً} [al-Nabaʾ: 38], because the context here requires the plural to precede the singular, since it is a context of intimidation and terrifying. «وكان مِقْدارُه» is an adjective of «يومَ», and the clause «تَعْرُجُ» is a fresh sentence.
His saying: {فِي يَوْمٍ}: There are two views. The more apparent is that it is attached to «تَعْرُجُ». The second is that it is attached to «دافعٌ», and on this view the clause «تَعْرُجُ الملائكةُ» is parenthetical. The pronoun in «إليه» apparently refers to Allah the Exalted. It was said that it refers to the place, as the circumstance and the context indicate it. The pronoun in «يَرَوْنه» and «نَراه» refers to the day, if the Day of Resurrection is meant by it. It was also said: to the punishment.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ تَكُونُ}: There are several views. First: that it is attached to «قريباً»; this is apparent when the pronoun in «نراه» refers to the punishment. Second: that it is attached to an omitted element indicated by «واقع», that is: "it will occur on the day when it will be." Third: that it is attached to an omitted element implied after it, that is: "on the day when it will be, such-and-such will happen." Fourth: that it is a badal (substitute) for the pronoun in «نَراه», if that refers to the Day of Resurrection. Fifth: that it is a badal for «في يومٍ» according to those who attach that to «واقع»; this was said by al-Zamakhsharī. He said "according to those who attach it to «واقع»" only because, if it is attached to «تَعْرُج», as in one of the two views given above, it is impossible for this to be a substitute for it, since the ascent of the angels does not take place on this day on which the sky is like molten brass and the mountains like carded wool, and every close friend is distracted from his close friend. The Shaykh said: "This is not permissible," meaning its substitution for «في يوم». He said: "Even though «في يوم» is in the position of the accusative, an accusative is not made a substitute for it, because a phrase like this is neither redundant nor treated as redundant, like «رُبَّ»; consideration of the position is permitted only with a redundant preposition, as in his saying:
4328 - أبَني لُبَيْنَى لَسْتُما بِيَدٍ ... إلاَّ يَداً ليسَتْ لها عَضُدُ
(O sons of Lubayna, you are not a hand, except a hand that has no forearm.) Likewise one cannot say «مَرَرْتُ بزيدٍ الخياطَ» on the position of «بزيدٍ», nor «مَرَرْتُ بزيدٍ وعمراً», nor «غَضِبْتُ على زيد وجعفراً», nor «مَرَرْتُ بعمروٍ أخاك», on the basis of consideration of the position." I say: it has already been mentioned that the reading {وامسحوا بِرُؤُوسِكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ} [al-Māʾida: 6] belongs to this category for those who read «الأرجل» in the accusative, so this would be like it; it has been discussed before, so I do not repeat it.
Then the Shaykh said: "If you say: the vowel in «يومَ تكون» is a vowel of indeclinability (mabnī), not a case vowel, so it is genitive like «في يومٍ», I say: it cannot be indeclinable according to the Basrans, because it is annexed to a declinable word; but it is permitted according to the Kufans, so al-Zamakhsharī's words go through on their school, if he had it in mind and intended it." End of quotation. His saying "if he had it in mind" contains an unfair attack on the man. What great matter is there in this that he would not have it in mind? Boasting about such a thing does not befit even some students, for it is among the well-known disputed questions, as famous as:
قِفا نَبْكِ. . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Halt, let us weep…) The discussion of المُهْل was given in al-Dukhān. As for العِهْن, it was said: wool in general; it was said: with the condition that it be red; it was said: with the condition that it be dyed; and it was said: with the condition that it be dyed in various colours. This last is the most fitting for the comparison, because the mountains are of varied colours, as the Exalted said: {جُدَدٌ بِيضٌ وَحُمْرٌ} [Fāṭir: 27].

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {وَلاَ يَسْأَلُ حَمِيمٌ}: The majority read «يَسْأَلُ» in the active voice. The second object is omitted. It was said that its implied form is: "he does not ask him for his help or his intercession, knowing that this is lacking." It was said: "he does not ask him for anything, such as bearing his burdens." It was said that «حميماً» is accusative by removal of the preposition, that is: "about a close friend," because he is preoccupied from him. Abū Jaʿfar, Abū Ḥaywa, Shayba and Ibn Kathīr in one transmission read «يُسْأل» in the passive. It was said that «حميماً» is a second object, not by removal of a preposition, the meaning being: "he is not asked to produce him." It was said instead that it is by removal of «عن», that is: "about a close friend."

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ}: It is made transitive to a second object by doubling (of the middle radical), and the first object stands in the place of the agent. As to the position of this clause there are two views. One: that it is in the position of an adjective of «حَميم». The other: that it is a fresh sentence. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the position of «يُبَصَّرُونهم»? I say: it is a fresh sentence, as though, when He said: «لا يَسْأل حَميمٌ حَميماً», it were said: 'Perhaps he does not see him.' So it was said: «يُبَصَّرُونهم»." Then he said: "It is also permissible that «يُبَصَّرُونهم» be an adjective, that is: close friends who are shown one another and made to recognise one another." End of quotation. The two pronouns in «يُبَصَّرُونهم», which refer to the two close friends, are in the plural only by being carried over to the sense of generality, because both are indefinite in the context of negation. Qatāda read «يُبْصِرُونهم» in the active voice, from «أَبْصَرَ», that is: the believer sees the unbeliever in the Fire. The reading of «يومئذٍ» with fatḥa and with kasra was discussed in Hūd. The majority annex «عذاب» to «يَوْمِئذ»; Abū Ḥaywa reads «العذاب» with tanwīn and «يَوْمئذٍ» in the accusative as an adverbial. The Shaykh said here: "The majority read it with kasra," that is, the mīm of «يومئذ», "and al-Aʿraj and Abū Ḥaywa with fatḥa." End of quotation. It has already been mentioned that the fatḥa is the reading of Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {وَفَصِيلَتِهِ}: Thaʿlab said: "الفصيلة: the nearest forefathers." Abū ʿUbayda said: "the thigh (i.e. the sub-clan)." It was said: his nearest kinsmen. This was mentioned before at His saying: {شُعُوباً وَقَبَآئِلَ} [al-Ḥujurāt: 13]. As for «تُؤْويه», al-Sūsī, from Abū ʿAmr, did not change the hamza (into a wāw); they said this is because it would lead to a word heavier than it, and the change is meant for lightening. al-Zuhrī read «تُؤْوِيْهُ» and «تُنْجِيْهُ» with a ḍamma on the pronoun hāʾ, which is the original form. «ثم يُنْجِيه» is conjoined to «يَفْتدي», so it falls within the scope of «لو»; the discussion of it has been given: is it a maṣdar-forming particle or a conditional about the past? The object of «يَوَدُّ» is omitted, that is: "he wishes for salvation." It was said that here it has the meaning of «إنْ» (if), but that is nothing. The agent of «يُنْجِيه» is either the pronoun of the ransoming, which «يَفْتدي» indicates, or the pronoun of those mentioned before, namely His saying {وَمَن فِي الأرض}. «مَنْ [في الأرض]» is genitive, conjoined to «بنيه» and what follows it, that is: "he wishes to ransom himself with {مَن في الأرض} as well." «جميعاً» is either a ḥāl (circumstantial) or tawkīd (emphasis), and it is singular in view of the form. «كَلاَّ» is a rebuke and a deterrent from believing that.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {إِنَّهَا لظى نَزَّاعَةً}: As to the pronoun there are three views. First: that it is the pronoun of the Fire, even though it has not been mentioned, because the word «عذاب» points to it. Second: that it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa). Third: that it is an indefinite pronoun that the predicate explains; this was said by al-Zamakhsharī. The investigation of that was given earlier at the saying of the Exalted: {إِنْ هِيَ إِلاَّ حَيَاتُنَا الدنيا}. On the first view, several possibilities arise for {لظى نَزَّاعَةً}: that «لَظى» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ», that is: "the Fire is Laẓā," with «نَزَّاعةٌ» a second khabar, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is: "it is a snatcher"; or that «لَظَى» is a badal (substitute) for the accusative pronoun and «نَزَّاعةٌ» is the khabar of «إنَّ». On the second view «لَظى نَزَّاعةٌ» is a clause made of a mubtadaʾ and khabar, in the position of nominative as the khabar of «إنَّ», explaining the pronoun of the matter; likewise on the third view. It is also permissible that «نَزَّاعةٌ» be an adjective of «لَظى», if you do not take it as a proper name but as meaning "flame"; the adjective is feminine, so «نَزَّاعةٌ» is said, because اللهَب means "fire". This was said by al-Zamakhsharī, and there is something to consider in it, because «لظى» is a diptote by agreement.
The Shaykh said, after relating the third view from al-Zamakhsharī: "I do not know what this indefinite pronoun is that the predicate explains. This is not one of the places in which a single word explains the pronoun, and had he not mentioned after this «or the pronoun of the matter», I would have taken his words in that sense." I say: whenever he makes it an indefinite pronoun it must be explained by a single word. That is either «لظى», with «نزاعةٌ» as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or «نزاعةٌ», with «لظى» as a badal for the pronoun, and this is nearer. It is not permissible that «لظى نَزَّاعةٌ» be a mubtadaʾ and khabar with the clause as the khabar of «إنَّ» while the pronoun is indefinite, so that the two views do not become identical, I mean this view and the view that it is the pronoun of the matter; for no pronoun is known to be explained by a clause except the pronoun of the affair and of the matter.
The nominative reading of «نَزَّاعَةٌ» is the reading of the majority. Ḥafṣ, Abū Ḥaywa, al-Zaʿfarānī, al-Yazīdī and Ibn Miqsam read «نَزَّاعَةً» in the accusative. It has two views. One: that it is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). As to its owner there are several views. One: that it is the latent pronoun in «لَظَى», because, although it is a proper name, it runs the course of derived words like al-Ḥārith and al-ʿAbbās, since it means التَّلَظِّي (blazing); and if the explicit proper name and the kunya operate on adverbials, then the proper name that runs the course of derived words is all the more fitting to operate on circumstantials. Among the occurrences of that is his saying:
4330 - أنا أبو المِنْهالِ بعضَ الأَحْيانْ
(I am Abū al-Minhāl, some of the time.) He made it include the meaning "I am the well known one at some times." Second: that it is the agent of «تَدْعو» and its ḥāl has been placed before it, that is: "she calls while being a snatcher." This ḥāl may be a corroborating one, because this is the nature of «لظى» and is known of its affair, or a transient one, because it is a matter known only by revelation. Third: that both it and the governing word are omitted, the implied form being: "she blazes, snatching," and «لَظَى» points to it.
The second of the first two views: that it is accusative on the basis of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ). al-Zamakhsharī expressed this as "terrifying", just as he expressed the nominative view as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being: "I mean a snatcher" and "I single her out." al-Mubarrad forbade the accusative of «نزاعة»; he said: "Because ḥāl is used only for what may be or may not be, and «لظى» is nothing but a snatcher." This is said in Makkī, who refuted him with the saying of the Exalted: {وَهُوَ الحق مُصَدِّقاً} [al-Baqara: 91] and {وهذا صِرَاطُ رَبِّكَ مُسْتَقِيماً} [al-Anʿām: 126]. He said: "The truth is nothing but confirming, and the path of your Lord is nothing but straight." I say: al-Mubarrad based the matter on the clarifying ḥāl, but that is not necessary, since the corroborating ḥāl has occurred, as Makkī adduced, even though it is contrary to the original rule.
اللَّظى originally means flame. It was transferred as a proper name for Gehenna, and for that reason it is a diptote. الشَّوى: the extremities, the plural of شَواة, like نَوى and نَواة. It was said that الشَّوى are the parts of the body that are not mortal spots; hence: «رماه فأَشْواه», that is, he did not hit his mortal spot. It was said that الشَّوى is the plural of شَواة, which is the skin of the head, and a verse of al-Aʿshā was recited:
433 - 1- قالت قُتَيْلَةُ مالَهُ ... قد جُلِّلَتْ شَيْباً شَواتُهْ
(Qutayla said: What is wrong with him? His scalp has been covered with grey hair.) [Translator's note: the source prints the verse number as "433 - 1-", evidently a corrupted form of 4331, following 4330; translated as written.] It was said: it is the skin of a human being. الشَّوى is also the worthless part of wealth, and the trivial thing. «تَدْعُو» may be the khabar of «إنَّ», or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or a ḥāl from «لَظى», or from «نَزَّاعة» according to the two readings of it, because it carries a pronoun.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {هَلُوعاً}: It is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of anticipated (muqaddara) kind. الهَلَع is explained by what follows it, namely His saying: «إذا» and «إذا». Thaʿlab said: "Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāhir asked me what الهَلَع is. I said: Allah has explained it, and there can be no clearer explanation than His: it is he who, when evil touches him, shows extreme impatience, and when good touches him, is miserly with it and withholds it from people." End of quotation. Its origin in the language, according to Abū ʿUbayd, is the most intense greed and the worst impatience. It was said: it is fright and swift agitation on being touched by something disliked, and swift withholding on being touched by good, from their saying «ناقةٌ هِلْواع», that is, a swift-travelling she-camel.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {جَزُوعاً}: and «مَنوعاً»: there are three views about them. First: that they are accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «هلُوعا», which is the governing word in them, the implied form being: "anxious (هَلُوعاً) while being impatient (جَزُوعاً) at the time evil touches him, and withholding (مَنوعاً) at the time good touches him." The two adverbials depend on these two ḥāls. Abū al-Baqāʾ expressed this view in a misleading phrase, though he means what I have mentioned, for he said: "«جَزُوعاً» is another ḥāl, and the governing word in it is «هَلُوعا»." His word "another" suggests that it is a second ḥāl and not a nested one, were it not for his saying "and the governing word in it is «هَلُوعا»." Second: that they are the two khabars (predicates) of an omitted kāna or ṣāra, that is: "when evil touches him he is or becomes impatient, and when good touches him he is or becomes withholding"; this was said by Makkī. On this view «إذا» is conditional, whereas on the first it is a pure adverbial, the governing word in it being what follows it, as stated above. Third: that they are an adjective of «هَلُوعا»; this was said by Makkī, except that he said: "There is some remoteness in it, because you intend to place it before «إذا»." End of quotation. This judgment of remoteness amounts to nothing, for the most that is in it is the placing of the adverbial before its governing word; what would be objectionable is placing what depends on the adjective before the described noun.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ المصلين}: It is an exception from «الإِنسان», since the genus is meant by it. Similar is: {إِنَّ الإنسان لَفِى خُسْرٍ إِلاَّ الذين آمَنُواْ} [al-ʿAṣr: 2-3].
Ḥafṣ read «بشهاداتِهم» in the plural, taking into account the multiplicity of kinds. The rest read it in the singular, since the genus is meant.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {عِزِينَ}: It is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «للذين كفروا». It was also said: a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مُهْطِعين», which would make it a nested ḥāl. «عن اليمين» may be attached to «عِزين», because it means "scattered"; this was said by Abū al-Baqāʾ. It may also be attached to «مُهْطِعين», that is: "hastening from these two directions." It may also be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, that is: "being on the right"; this was said by Abū al-Baqāʾ. عِزِين is the plural of «عِزَة», and العِزَة means a group. Makkī said: "It is pluralised with wāw and nūn, although it is feminine and not rational, because that is a compensation for what was dropped from it. It was said that its origin is عِزْهَة, just as the origin of سَنَة is سَنْهَة, and then the hāʾ was dropped." End of quotation. His saying "not rational" is a slip, because what counts is what the word denotes, and what it denotes is undoubtedly rational beings.
They disagreed about the lām (final radical) of «عِزَة» in three views. First: that it is wāw, from «عَزَوْتُه أَعْزُوْه», that is, "I ascribed him"; this is because the one ascribed is joined to the one to whom he is ascribed, just as every group is joined in its parts to one another. Second: that it is yāʾ, since one says «عَزَيْتُه» with yāʾ, «أَعْزِيْهِ», in the sense of «عَزَوْته»; on this view there are two dialects for its lām. Third: that it is hāʾ, and it takes a broken plural «عِزَىً», like كِسْرة and كِسَر, and this broken plural dispensed with its pluralisation by alif and tāʾ, so they did not say «عِزات», just as they did not say, for شَفَة and أَمَة, «شِفات» or «إمات», being content with «شِفاهٍ» and «إماءٍ»; and its occurrence pluralised with wāw and nūn is very frequent. al-Rāʿī said:
4332 - أخليفةَ الرحمنِ إنَّ عَشيرتي ... أَمسَوْا سَوامُهُمُ عِزِيْنَ فُلُوْلا
(O caliph of the Merciful, my kinsmen have come to evening with their herds scattered in groups and broken.) And al-Kumayt said:
4333 - ونحن وجَنْدَلٌ باغٍ تَرَكْنا ... كتائبَ جَنْدَلٍ شَتَّى عِزِيْنا
(We and Jandal the rebel left the squadrons of Jandal scattered in groups.) And ʿAntara said:
4334 - وقِرنٍ قد تَرَكْتُ لِذي وَلِيٍّ ... عليه الطيرُ كالعُصَبِ العِزِيْن
(And many an opponent I have left for the one who inherits him, with the birds over him like scattered bands.) And another said:
4335 - ترانا عنده والليلُ داجٍ ... على أبوابِه حِلَقاً عِزِيْنا
(You see us at his door while the night is dark, circles in groups.) And another said:
4336 - فلما أَنْ أَتَيْنَ على أُضاخٍ ... تَرَكْنَ حَصاه أَشْتاتاً عِزينا
(When they came upon Uḍākh, they left its pebbles scattered in groups.)
العِزَة in the language is a group that is dispersed. This is the statement of Abū ʿUbayda. al-Aṣmaʿī said: "العِزُون are kinds. One says: in the house there are عِزُون, that is, kinds." Another said: a small group such as three or four. al-Rāghib said: "It was said that it comes from their saying «عَزِيَ عَزاءً فهو عَزٍ» when he was patient, and «تَعَزَّى» means he was patient, so it is as though it were a name for the group whose members console one another."

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {أَن يُدْخَلَ}: The majority read it in the passive. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Yaʿmur, Abū Rajāʾ and ʿĀṣim in one transmission read it in the active.

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ}: This has been discussed more than once. A group read «فلأُقْسِمُ» without an alif. The majority read the plural «المَشارق والمغارب»; al-Jaḥdarī and Ibn Muḥayṣin read both in the singular.
«إنَّا لَقادِرون» is the answer to the oath. The majority read «يُلاقُوا»; Abū Jaʿfar and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «يَلْقَوْا», the imperfect of «لَقِيَ».

semin-durr:43-43.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ}: It may be a badal (substitute) for «يَوْمَهم», or accusative by an omitted «أعني» ("I mean"). According to the view of the Kufans it may be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject) and be built on fatḥa (mabnī), even though it is annexed to a declinable word, that is: "it is the day they will come out", as in His saying: {هذا يَوْمُ يَنفَعُ}; the discussion of it has already been given fully. The majority read «يَخْرُجون» in the active; a passive reading is transmitted from ʿĀṣim.
His saying: {سِرَاعاً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يَخْرُجون»; it is the plural of سريع, like ظِراف from ظَريف. «كأنَّهم» is a ḥāl from the pronoun of the ḥāl, so it is a nested one.
His saying: {إلى نُصُبٍ}: attached to the khabar. The majority read «نَصْبٍ» with fatḥa and sukūn; Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ with two ḍammas; Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī and Mujāhid with two fatḥas; al-Ḥasan and Qatāda with ḍamma and sukūn. The first is a singular noun meaning the erected standard toward which a person hastens. Abū ʿAmr said: "It is the hunter's net, to which he hastens when game falls into it, fearing that it will escape." As for the second, it admits three views. One: that it is a singular noun meaning the idol set up for worship, and a verse of al-Aʿshā was recited:
4337 - وذا النُّصُبَ المَنْصُوبَ لا تَعْبُدَنَّه ... لعاقبةٍ واللَّهَ ربَّك فاعْبُدَا
(Do not worship that erected idol with a view to the outcome, but worship Allah your Lord.) Two: that it is the plural of نِصاب, like كُتُب from كِتاب. Three: that it is the plural of نَصْبٍ, like رُهُن from رَهْن and سُقُف from سَقْف; this is the statement of Abū al-Ḥasan. The plural of the plural is أَنْصاب. As for the third, it is the form فَعَل in the sense of مَفْعول, that is, "set up", like القَبَض and النَّقَض. The fourth is a lightening of the second. «يُوْفِضون» means "they hasten". It was said: "they race one another"; it was said: "they run"; it was said: "they set out." These are close in meaning. He recited:
4338 - فوارِسُ ذُبْيانَ تحت الحَدِيْ ... دِ كالجِنِّ تُوْفِضُ مِنْ عَبْقَرِ
(The horsemen of Dhubyān, under the iron, like the jinn hastening from ʿAbqar.) And another said:
4339 - لأَنعتَنْ نَعامةً مِيفاضا ... خَرْجاءَ [تَعْدُو] تَطْلُبُ الإِضاضا
(I shall describe an ostrich, a swift one, speckled black and white, running, seeking a refuge.) that is, a hastening one.
